definition_zh: adv./adj. 迷路；走失；偏离正道；误入歧途；出岔子
definition_en: Away from the right path or the intended place, so that something is lost; into error or bad behaviour, so that someone is misled.
core_image: 本该沿这条路走，脚却拐进了旁边的荒草里
scene: 那封信在邮路中途不知去了哪里。The letter went astray somewhere in the post.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：astray 指偏离应在的路线或位置，go astray 就是「走失、丢了」。

forms.label: 副词与表语形容词（无屈折变化）

senses.title: Off the intended path
senses.definition: away from the right route or place, so that a person, animal or thing is lost
senses.definitionCN: 离开正确的路线或位置，以致人、动物或东西走失
senses.example: Two sheep had gone astray in the fog.
senses.exampleCN: 两只羊在雾里走失了。
senses.why: The root means to wander outside a boundary, so the word always implies a line that should have been kept.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「在边界之外游荡」，所以这个词总暗示着一条本该守住却没有守住的线。

senses.title: Into error or bad behaviour
senses.definition: into mistake or wrongdoing, especially because someone or something misleads you
senses.definitionCN: 陷入错误或坏事，尤指被人或事误导
senses.example: Bad advice led the whole team astray.
senses.exampleCN: 糟糕的建议把整个团队带偏了。
senses.why: The path becomes a metaphor for conduct, which is why lead astray is the commonest phrase in this sense.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「路」变成了品行的隐喻，所以 lead astray 是这个义项最常见的说法。

intro.en: Astray is a-, on or in, plus stray, from Old French estraier, from a Vulgar Latin compound of extra, outside, and vagari, to wander.
intro.cn: astray 是 a-「在……上」加 stray，后者来自古法语 estraier，再往上是通俗拉丁语由 extra「在外」与 vagari「游荡」拼成的复合词。

items.en: Latin extra meant outside or beyond, the boundary part of the word.
items.cn: 拉丁语 extra 意为「在外、越过」，提供这个词的「边界」部分。

items.en: Latin vagari meant to wander about, and gives vagrant and vague.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vagari 意为「四处游荡」，产生 vagrant 与 vague。

items.en: The compound meant to wander outside the proper bounds, used of straying animals.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为「越出应有范围游荡」，用于走失的牲畜。

items.en: Old French estraier kept the sense of wandering off, and English clipped its opening to stray.
items.cn: 古法语 estraier 保留「走开去」的意思，英语把开头截掉成了 stray。

items.en: Middle English added the prefix a-, on, giving astray as an adverb of state.
items.cn: 中古英语加上前缀 a-「在……上」，构成表状态的副词 astray。

items.en: Preachers quickly used the word for conduct, so leading a soul astray became a standard image.
items.cn: 布道者很快把这个词用于品行，「把灵魂引入歧途」成了固定意象。

note.en: The look-alike group separates astray from ashtray and array, which only sound alike; the near-meaning group grades ways of being off course.
note.cn: 形近组把 astray 与只是音近的 ashtray、array 分开；近义组按程度区分各种「偏离」。

entries.definition: To wander away from the group.
entries.definitionCN: 从群体中走开去。

entries.definition: A small dish for cigarette ash.
entries.definitionCN: 盛烟灰的小碟。

entries.definition: An ordered collection set out in rows.
entries.definitionCN: 成行摆开的一大批东西。

entries.definition: A domestic animal found wandering.
entries.definitionCN: 被发现走失的家畜。

entries.definition: Floating without direction or control.
entries.definitionCN: 随水漂着，无方向无控制。

entries.definition: Away from the intended route.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离既定航线。

entries.definition: Wrong, not as it should be.
entries.definitionCN: 不对头，与本应如此不同。

entries.definition: Unable to find the way or the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 找不到路或找不到东西。

normalIntro.en: Astray is a- plus stray: on the wander, outside the line you should have kept.
normalIntro.cn: astray 就是 a- 加 stray：处在游荡状态，越出了本该守住的那条线。

normal.en: Go astray is used of things and of people.
normal.cn: go astray 既用于东西也用于人。

normal.en: Lead someone astray needs an object.
normal.cn: lead someone astray 必须带宾语。

normal.en: Astray follows the verb, never a noun.
normal.cn: astray 跟在动词后，不放在名词前。

normal.en: Stray, vagrant and vague share the root.
normal.cn: stray、vagrant、vague 共用这个词根。

normal.en: Ashtray is ash plus tray, quite unrelated.
normal.cn: ashtray 是 ash 加 tray，毫无亲缘。

abstract.en: Picture footsteps leaving the path for the grass.
abstract.cn: 想象脚印离开小径拐进草地。

abstract.en: Imagine a letter sitting in the wrong sack.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信躺在错误的邮袋里。

abstract.en: Think of a compass needle pulled off north.
abstract.cn: 想象一根被拽离北向的罗盘针。

examples.en: The parcel went astray in December.
examples.cn: 那个包裹在十二月寄丢了。

examples.en: He was led astray by older boys.
examples.cn: 他被几个大孩子带坏了。

examples.en: Even careful plans can go astray.
examples.cn: 再周密的计划也可能出岔子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「在……上」+ stray「走失」——正处在走丢的状态，就是 astray。

root: 拉丁语 extra「在外」加 vagari「游荡」构成通俗拉丁语「越界游荡」，经古法语 estraier 截头成 stray，中古英语加 a- 成 astray；同根还有 vagrant 与 vague。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses leave a line: a path you should have stayed on, and a standard of conduct you should have kept.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都离开了一条线：本该走的那条路，以及本该守的那份行为准则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet turning off the path into the grass
core.cn: 核心意象：本该沿这条路走，脚却拐进了旁边的荒草里

branches.en: Sheep wandering in the fog.
A letter in the wrong sack.
Advice pulling a team off course.
Older boys leading a child wrong.
Both cross a line that should hold.
branches.cn: 两者都越过了本该守住的线。

intro.en: Astray is a-, on, plus stray; the wandering root vag- builds vagrant, vague and extravagant, all words for leaving bounds.
intro.cn: astray 是 a-「在……上」加 stray；「游荡」词根 vag- 构成 vagrant、vague 与 extravagant，都是「越界」的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is extra, outside, vagari, to wander, and vagus, roaming; the prefix a- is English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 extra「在外」、vagari「游荡」与 vagus「漫游的」；前缀 a- 属英语。

latinEntries.exampleCN: vagari 产生 vagrant 与 vague。
vagus 指那条「游走的」神经。

definition_zh: n. 占星师；星占家（同 astrologer）；旧时宫廷星官
definition_en: A person who practises astrology, reading the positions of stars and planets to judge human affairs; historically, a court official who did this.
core_image: 一张星盘摊在桌上，手指按着某颗星替人断事
scene: 国王派人请来星官为出征择日。The king sent for an astrologist to choose the day.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：astrologist 指以星象推断人事的人，与 astrologer 同义。

senses.title: A person who reads the stars
senses.definition: someone who interprets star and planet positions to advise on human affairs, the same as an astrologer
senses.definitionCN: 解读星体位置以指点人事的人，与 astrologer 同义
senses.example: The astrologist drew a chart for the newborn child.
senses.exampleCN: 占星师为新生儿排了一张星盘。
senses.why: The ending -ist marks a practitioner, so the word names the person rather than the belief system.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ist 标示从业者，所以这个词指的是人，而不是那套信仰体系。

senses.title: A court officer of the old kind
senses.definition: in earlier courts, an official who kept calendars and read omens for the ruler, before the split from astronomy
senses.definitionCN: 旧时宫廷中为君主掌历法、读天象征兆的官员，存在于与天文学分家之前
senses.example: The court astrologist also kept the calendar.
senses.exampleCN: 这位宫廷星官同时掌管历法。
senses.why: Before the seventeenth century the roles overlapped, so the same person measured the sky and read its meaning.
senses.whyCN: 十七世纪之前两种角色重叠，所以同一个人既测量天空，也解读它的含义。

intro.en: Astrologist is astrology plus -ist, from Greek astrologia, star account, from aster, star, and logos, word or reckoning, through Latin astrologus.
intro.cn: astrologist 就是 astrology 加 -ist，词源为希腊语 astrologia「星的记述」，由 aster「星」与 logos「言说、推算」构成，经拉丁语 astrologus 传入。

items.en: Greek aster meant star, the first half of every word in this family.
items.cn: 希腊语 aster 意为「星」，是这个词族每个词的前半。

items.en: Greek logos meant word, account or reckoning, so the compound meant an account of the stars.
items.cn: 希腊语 logos 意为「言说、记述、推算」，所以这个复合词意为「关于星的记述」。

items.en: Greek astrologia covered both measuring the heavens and reading their meaning for human lives.
items.cn: 希腊语 astrologia 同时涵盖测量天象与解读其对人事的含义。

items.en: Latin astrologus named the practitioner, and medieval courts kept such officers.
items.cn: 拉丁语 astrologus 指从业者，中世纪宫廷养着这样的官员。

items.en: English preferred astrologer for centuries, using -er for the same practitioner.
items.cn: 英语数百年来偏用 astrologer，用 -er 指同一类从业者。

items.en: The form astrologist spread later, and the seventeenth-century split from astronomy left it clearly on the belief side.
items.cn: astrologist 这一形式后来才流行；十七世纪与天文学分家后，它明确留在信仰一侧。

note.en: The look-alike group contrasts the two endings for the same job and the neighbouring science; the near-meaning group lists other readers of hidden signs.
note.cn: 形近组对比同一职业的两种后缀以及邻近的那门科学；近义组列出其他解读隐秘征兆的人。

entries.definition: A person who practises astrology.
entries.definitionCN: 从事占星的人。

entries.definition: A scientist who studies celestial bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 研究天体的科学家。

entries.definition: A specialist in the earth and its rocks.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地球与岩石的专家。

entries.definition: A specialist in mind and behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 研究心理与行为的专家。

entries.definition: Someone who reads hidden signs.
entries.definitionCN: 解读隐秘征兆的人。

entries.definition: Someone who claims to foretell a life.
entries.definitionCN: 声称能预知命运的人。

entries.definition: A person believed to see what is hidden.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为能看见隐秘之事的人。

entries.definition: Someone who watches the stars, often idly.
entries.definitionCN: 望星的人，常带闲看意味。

normalIntro.en: Astrologist is astro-, star, plus -logist, one who studies: a star reader, not a star measurer.
normalIntro.cn: astrologist 就是 astro-「星」加 -logist「研究者」：读星的人，而不是量星的人。

normal.en: Astrologer and astrologist mean the same job.
normal.cn: astrologer 与 astrologist 指同一职业。

normal.en: Astronomer is the scientist, not the reader.
normal.cn: astronomer 是科学家，不是解读者。

normal.en: The ending -ist marks a practitioner.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ist 标示从业者。

normal.en: Astrology is the practice, astrologist the person.
normal.cn: astrology 是术，astrologist 是人。

normal.en: Court astrologists once kept calendars too.
normal.cn: 宫廷星官从前还兼管历法。

abstract.en: Picture a finger resting on one star of a chart.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指按在星盘的某颗星上。

abstract.en: Imagine a ruler waiting for a lucky date.
abstract.cn: 想象一位君主等着一个吉日。

abstract.en: Think of a calendar and an omen in one ledger.
abstract.cn: 想象同一本册子里既记历法也记征兆。

examples.en: The astrologist warned against travel that month.
examples.cn: 占星师劝那个月不要远行。

examples.en: Two astrologists gave opposite readings.
examples.cn: 两位占星师给出相反的解读。

examples.en: She works as an astrologist for a magazine.
examples.cn: 她为一家杂志做占星师。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：astro「星」+ log「说」+ -ist「人」——替星星说话的人，就是占星师 astrologist。

root: 希腊语 aster「星」加 logos「记述」构成 astrologia，拉丁语 astrologus 指从业者；英语先有 astrologer，后加 -ist 成 astrologist，十七世纪与 astronomy 分道。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one reader of the sky: the modern practitioner with a chart, and the old court officer who also kept the calendar.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是同一位读天者：拿着星盘的现代从业者，以及兼管历法的旧时宫廷官员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a star chart open, a finger pressing one point to judge a life
core.cn: 核心意象：一张星盘摊在桌上，手指按着某颗星替人断事

branches.en: A chart drawn for a newborn.
Two readers, opposite readings.
branches.cn: 两位解读者，相反的结论。

branches.en: A ruler waiting for a lucky date.
A calendar and omens in one book.
One sky read for meaning, not measured.
branches.cn: 同一片天，被解读含义而非测量。

intro.en: Astrologist is astro- plus -logy plus -ist; the same layers build astronomy, geologist and psychologist.
intro.cn: astrologist 是 astro- 加 -logy 再加 -ist；同样的层次还构成 astronomy、geologist 与 psychologist。

latinIntro.en: The classical layer is Greek aster, star, and logos, account, matched by Latin astrum and ratio; astrologus named the practitioner.
latinIntro.cn: 古典层次是希腊语 aster「星」与 logos「记述」，对应拉丁语 astrum 与 ratio；astrologus 指从业者。

latinEntries.exampleCN: astrologus 产生表示人的名词。

definition_zh: n. 占星术（以天体位置推断人事的信仰体系）；某一具体的占星传统
definition_en: The belief system that reads the positions of stars and planets as signs of human character and events; also one particular tradition of that practice.
core_image: 十二个符号围成一圈，把人的命运挂在星位上
scene: 她一边吃早饭一边看报纸角落的星座运势。She reads the astrology column over breakfast.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：astrology 指以星象推断人事的那套信仰体系，即占星术。

senses.title: The practice of reading stars
senses.definition: the belief that star and planet positions reveal character and foretell events, treated as one body of practice
senses.definitionCN: 认为星体位置揭示性格并预示事件的信仰，作为一整套术来看待
senses.example: Astrology has no support from controlled tests.
senses.exampleCN: 占星术得不到对照试验的支持。
senses.why: The ending -logy once meant any account of a subject, so the word claimed the same standing as a science.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -logy 曾指任何一门关于某主题的记述，所以这个词一度自称与科学同等地位。

senses.title: One tradition of that practice
senses.definition: a particular system with its own signs and rules, such as Western or Chinese astrology
senses.definitionCN: 有自己符号与规则的某一体系，如西方占星或中国占星
senses.example: The two astrologies use different animal cycles.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种占星传统使用不同的生肖循环。
senses.why: Once the practice spread across cultures, the noun became countable, naming each system separately.
senses.whyCN: 这套术跨文化传播后，名词变得可数，用来分别指称各个体系。

intro.en: Astrology is Greek astrologia, from aster, star, and logos, account: an account of the stars, a term that once covered astronomy as well.
intro.cn: astrology 就是希腊语 astrologia，由 aster「星」与 logos「记述」构成：关于星的记述，这个术语曾把天文学也包括在内。

items.en: Greek aster meant star, and gives every member of this word family its first half.
items.cn: 希腊语 aster 意为「星」，给这个词族的每个成员提供前半部分。

items.en: Greek logos meant word, reason or account, the ending that later came to mean a field of study.
items.cn: 希腊语 logos 意为「言说、理性、记述」，这个后缀后来表示一门学问。

items.en: In Greek the compound covered both careful observation of the heavens and interpretation of their meaning.
items.cn: 在希腊语中，这个复合词同时涵盖对天象的细致观测与对其含义的解读。

items.en: Latin kept the double sense, so medieval writers used it for what we now call astronomy.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留了双重含义，所以中世纪作者用它指今天所说的天文学。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century, still covering both measurement and divination.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个词，当时仍兼指测量与占卜。

items.en: Seventeenth-century science kept astronomy for measurement and left astrology for the belief, fixing the modern contrast.
items.cn: 十七世纪的科学把「测量」留给 astronomy，把「信仰」留给 astrology，固定了今天的对立。

note.en: The look-alike group sets the science beside the belief and adds two other -logy fields; the near-meaning group lists neighbouring sign systems.
note.cn: 形近组把科学与信仰并置，并加上另外两门 -logy 学问；近义组列出邻近的符号体系。

entries.definition: The scientific study of celestial bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 对天体的科学研究。

entries.definition: Relating to the reading of stars.
entries.definitionCN: 与读星断事有关的。

entries.definition: The study of the earth and its rocks.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地球与岩石的学问。

entries.definition: The study of religious belief.

entries.definition: A reading drawn from star positions.
entries.definitionCN: 依星位排出的运势解读。

entries.definition: Any attempt to read hidden signs.
entries.definitionCN: 一切解读隐秘征兆的做法。

entries.definition: The band of twelve signs used in star reading.

entries.definition: Reading meaning into numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 把含义读进数字里的术。

normalIntro.en: Astrology is astro-, star, plus -logy, account: an account of the stars that claims to read human lives.
normalIntro.cn: astrology 就是 astro-「星」加 -logy「记述」：一份关于星的记述，却声称能读出人的命运。

normal.en: Astronomy measures, astrology interprets.
normal.cn: astronomy 测量，astrology 解读。

normal.en: Uncountable for the practice, plural for traditions.
normal.cn: 指这门术时不可数，指传统时可数。

normal.en: Astrologer and astrologist name the person.
normal.cn: astrologer 与 astrologist 指人。

normal.en: Astrological is the adjective.
normal.cn: astrological 是形容词。

normal.en: The two words were one until the 1600s.
normal.cn: 这两个词在十七世纪前本是一个。

abstract.en: Picture twelve signs arranged in a ring.
abstract.cn: 想象十二个符号围成一圈。

abstract.en: Imagine a newspaper corner predicting your week.
abstract.cn: 想象报纸一角预测你这一周。

abstract.en: Think of a birth moment turned into a chart.
abstract.cn: 想象一个出生时刻被排成一张盘。

examples.en: She studies astrology as a hobby.
examples.cn: 她把占星当爱好来研习。

examples.en: Astrology was once part of university teaching.
examples.cn: 占星术曾是大学教学的一部分。

examples.en: The book compares several astrologies.
examples.cn: 这本书比较了几种占星传统。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：astro「星」+ -logy「学问」——把星象当成一门学问来读人事，就是占星术 astrology。

root: 希腊语 aster「星」加 logos「记述」构成 astrologia，经拉丁语入十四世纪英语，原兼指天象测量与占卜；十七世纪分家后专指占星信仰。

sensesIntro.en: The two senses are one practice seen twice: the whole belief system, and each cultural version of it with its own signs.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一套术被看了两遍：整个信仰体系，以及各有符号的文化版本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: twelve signs in a ring, a life hung on star positions
core.cn: 核心意象：十二个符号围成一圈，把人的命运挂在星位上

branches.en: A newspaper column predicting a week.
branches.cn: 预测一周运势的报纸专栏。

branches.en: A birth moment turned into a chart.
branches.cn: 被排成星盘的出生时刻。

branches.en: Twelve animals in one tradition.
branches.cn: 某一传统里的十二种动物。

branches.en: Two systems, different cycles.
Reading meaning into the sky.

intro.en: Astrology is astro- plus -logy; the same ending builds geology, theology and numerology, while astronomy took -nomy instead.
intro.cn: astrology 是 astro- 加 -logy；同一后缀构成 geology、theology 与 numerology，而 astronomy 改用 -nomy。

latinIntro.en: The classical layer is Greek aster, star, and logos, account, matched by Latin astrum and ratio; astrologia held both senses.
latinIntro.cn: 古典层次是希腊语 aster「星」与 logos「记述」，对应拉丁语 astrum 与 ratio；astrologia 曾兼含两义。

latinEntries.exampleCN: ratio 产生 reason 与 ration。

definition_zh: 宇航员；航天员；航天飞行乘组成员
definition_en: a person who is trained to travel and work in a spacecraft
core_image: 一个穿着白色宇航服的人被绑进座椅，身后是火箭尾焰和漆黑天空
scene: 电视直播里主持人激动地说：The astronaut floated into the space station and waved at the camera.
sceneCN: 这里指「乘航天器进入太空的人」（第 1 个义项：接受训练乘航天器上太空的人）；句意为宇航员飘进空间站，对着镜头挥手。

pos.zh: 宇航员；航天员；乘航天器进入太空的人

derivatives.zh: 天文学家（共享 astro- 词根，但研究而非飞行）

senses.title: A trained space traveler
senses.titleCN: 受训乘航天器进入太空的人
senses.definition: a person trained by a space program to travel and work aboard a spacecraft
senses.definitionCN: 由航天计划训练、乘航天器进入太空并在其上工作的人
senses.example: The astronaut spent six months aboard the space station.
senses.exampleCN: 这位宇航员在空间站上待了六个月。
senses.why: The word literally means 'star sailor': someone who sails among the stars, so the core image is a person riding a craft through space.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面意思是「星际水手」：在群星间航行的人，所以核心意象是乘飞行器穿越太空的人。

senses.title: A crew member of a space mission
senses.definition: one of the people assigned to fly a particular space mission, whether pilot, scientist or engineer
senses.definitionCN: 被指派执行某次航天飞行任务的人员，无论担任飞行员、科学家还是工程师
senses.example: Each astronaut on the mission had a different job during launch.
senses.exampleCN: 任务中每位宇航员在发射时承担不同的职责。
senses.why: Spacecraft carry crews like ships carry sailors, so astronaut extends to every member of that crew.
senses.whyCN: 航天器像船载水手一样载着乘组，所以 astronaut 扩展到乘组的每一位成员。

senses.title: A national space program title
senses.definition: the English term for space travelers of the US and international programs, contrasted with cosmonaut and taikonaut
senses.definitionCN: 美国及国际计划中航天员的英语称谓，与俄语 cosmonaut、中文 taikonaut 相对
senses.example: An American astronaut and a Russian cosmonaut shared the same capsule.
senses.exampleCN: 一位美国宇航员和一位俄罗斯宇航员共用同一个返回舱。
senses.why: Different space agencies coined their own words from the same Greek roots, so astronaut names one tradition among several.
senses.whyCN: 各国航天机构用同一批希腊词根造了自己的词，astronaut 只是其中一种传统的称呼。

senses.title: A job or career in spaceflight
senses.definition: the profession of flying in space, requiring years of training in engineering, science and survival
senses.definitionCN: 上太空执行飞行任务的职业，需要在工程、科学和生存训练上投入多年
senses.example: She dreamed of becoming an astronaut since primary school.
senses.exampleCN: 她从小学起就梦想成为宇航员。
senses.why: Because training is long and selective, astronaut also names the career itself, like pilot or sailor.
senses.whyCN: 由于训练漫长且选拔严格，astronaut 也像 pilot、sailor 一样指这份职业本身。

senses.title: Figurative use for a space-like experience
senses.titleCN: 比喻用法：仿佛置身太空的人
senses.definition: informally, someone in a situation that feels weightless, isolated or otherworldly
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，指处于失重、隔绝或仿佛在另一个世界的人
senses.example: With all the noise cancelling on, I felt like an astronaut in my own bubble.
senses.exampleCN: 开着降噪耳机，我感觉自己像置身太空泡泡里的宇航员。
senses.why: The image of a lone figure floating in a white suit is so vivid that people borrow it for any isolated, floating experience.
senses.whyCN: 白色宇航服里孤独漂浮的形象太鲜明，人们借它形容任何隔绝、漂浮般的处境。

senses.title: Historic and pioneer astronauts
senses.definition: people remembered as the first or most famous space travelers, such as Yuri Gagarin or Neil Armstrong
senses.definitionCN: 作为最早或最著名航天者被记住的人，如加加林、阿姆斯特朗
senses.example: Schoolchildren learn the name of the first astronaut who orbited the Earth.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们都要学习第一位绕地球飞行的宇航员的名字。
senses.why: Because spaceflight is young, each milestone astronaut is a named hero in history books.
senses.whyCN: 航天历史很短，每个里程碑式的宇航员都成了史册上有名有姓的英雄。

senses.title: Astronaut in training or candidates
senses.definition: applicants and trainees who have been selected for a space program but have not yet flown
senses.definitionCN: 已被航天计划选中但尚未上天的候选人和受训者
senses.example: The new class of astronaut candidates begins underwater training next month.
senses.exampleCN: 新一届宇航员候选人下月开始水下训练。
senses.why: Selection is so famous that even people who have never left Earth are already called astronauts in the media.
senses.whyCN: 选拔过程太出名，媒体把还没离开地球的受训者就已经称作宇航员。

senses.title: Everyday and childhood usage
senses.definition: used loosely by children or in play for anyone in a space costume or dreaming of space
senses.definitionCN: 孩子游戏或口语中，泛指穿太空服、向往太空的任何人
senses.example: The toddler in a puffy snowsuit waddled across the room like a little astronaut.
senses.exampleCN: 穿着蓬松雪地服的幼儿像小宇航员一样摇摇摆摆地穿过房间。
senses.why: The costume defines the image, so anything bulky and white invites the nickname astronaut.
senses.whyCN: 服装本身定义了形象，任何白色臃肿的装束都会让人联想到宇航员。

intro.en: astronaut is a modern coinage from Greek astro- (star) and naut- (sailor), literally 'star sailor', modeled on words like aeronaut.
intro.cn: astronaut 是现代造词，来自希腊语 astro-（星）和 naut-（水手），字面义为「星际水手」，仿照 aeronaut 一类词构成。

items.en: Greek astron means 'star' and nautes means 'sailor'; neither formed a classical compound astronaut.
items.cn: 希腊语 astron 意为「星」，nautes 意为「水手」；古希腊语中并没有 astronaut 这样的复合词。

items.en: In the 1920s to 1930s, writers coined astronaut on the model of aeronaut, a balloon traveler of the 18th and 19th centuries.
items.cn: 二十世纪二三十年代，作家们仿照十八九世纪的热气球旅行者 aeronaut，造出了 astronaut 一词。

items.en: Early English uses referred to fictional or imagined space travelers before any real spaceflight existed.
items.cn: 在真实航天出现之前，英语里的 astronaut 最早指小说和想象中的太空旅行者。

items.en: After Gagarin's flight in 1961 and the US Mercury program, astronaut became the official title for American space travelers.
items.cn: 1961 年加加林升空及美国水星计划之后，astronaut 成为美国航天员的正式称谓。

items.en: The Soviet program used cosmonaut (kosmos + nautes) and China later used taikonaut, all built on the same sailor image.
items.cn: 苏联计划用 cosmonaut（宇宙 + 水手），中国后来用 taikonaut（太空 + 水手），都基于同一「航行」意象。

items.en: Today astronaut is the general English word for any professional space traveler, whatever their nationality.
items.cn: 今天 astronaut 是英语中对职业航天员的通称，不问国籍。

note.en: Group one collects astro- words that look or build alike; group two collects near-meaning space traveler terms.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或同用 astro- 词根的词；第二组是语义相近的太空旅行者称谓。

entries.definition: A scientist who studies the stars; shares astro- but studies from Earth rather than flying.
entries.definitionCN: 研究星辰的科学家；共享 astro- 词根，但在地面研究而非上天飞行。

entries.definition: The science of celestial objects; the field an astronaut may fly for but is not itself a person.
entries.definitionCN: 研究天体的学科；宇航员可能为之飞行，但它本身不是人。

entries.definition: One who reads horoscopes; looks close to astronomer but is not a science profession.
entries.definitionCN: 看星盘占卜的人；与 astronomer 拼写相近，但并非科学职业。

entries.definition: The Russian and Soviet term for a space traveler, built on kosmos instead of astron.
entries.definitionCN: 俄苏航天员的称谓，用 kosmos 而非 astron 构词。

entries.definition: The English word for Chinese space travelers, from taikong (space) plus naut.
entries.definitionCN: 中国航天员的英文称谓，来自「太空」加 naut。

entries.definition: Flies aircraft within the atmosphere; an astronaut pilots spacecraft beyond it.
entries.definitionCN: 在大气层内驾驶飞机；宇航员在大气层外驾驶航天器。

normalIntro.en: Remember astronaut as a sailor of the stars: astro- star + naut sailor.
normalIntro.cn: 把 astronaut 记成「星际水手」：astro- 星 + naut 水手。

normal.en: astro- means star, as in astronomy; naut means sailor, as in nautical.
normal.cn: astro- 表示星（如 astronomy）；naut 表示水手（如 nautical 航海的）。

normal.en: cosmonaut and taikonaut share the same -naut tail; only the first part changes by country.
normal.cn: cosmonaut、taikonaut 共用 -naut 尾，只有前半随国家不同。

normal.en: An astronaut trains for years before riding a rocket.
normal.cn: 宇航员上天前要训练好几年。

normal.en: aeronaut (balloon sailor) was the model for astronaut.
normal.cn: aeronaut（气球水手）是 astronaut 的构词蓝本。

normal.en: Think of a white spacesuit floating outside the space station.
normal.cn: 想象空间站外漂浮的一袭白色宇航服。

abstract.en: A tiny white figure drifting above a blue marble that holds everyone you know.
abstract.cn: 小小的白色身影，漂浮在容纳你所有熟人的蓝色圆球之上。

abstract.en: The silence of a helmet: your own breath is the loudest sound.
abstract.cn: 头盔里的寂静：自己的呼吸是最响的声音。

abstract.en: A rope between you and the ship — the only thread home.
abstract.cn: 你和飞船之间的一根系绳——回家唯一的线。

examples.en: The astronaut answered questions from students while floating in zero gravity.
examples.cn: 宇航员在失重漂浮中回答了学生们的问题。

examples.en: Only the healthiest candidates are chosen to become astronauts.
examples.cn: 只有最健康的候选人才能被选为宇航员。

examples.en: Astronauts must exercise daily to keep their muscles strong in orbit.
examples.cn: 宇航员在轨道上必须每天锻炼以保持肌肉力量。

dict_mnemonic.text: astro-（星）+ naut（水手）= 星际水手 = 宇航员

root: 希腊语 astron（星）+ nautes（水手）→ 现代仿 aeronaut 造词 astronaut。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from one image, a person sailing among the stars: the trained traveler, the mission crew, national titles, the career, figurative use, historic pioneers, trainees and playful usage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由「星际航行的人」这一意象展开：受训的旅行者、任务乘组、各国称谓、职业、比喻用法、历史先驱、受训者、童趣用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white-suited sailor floating in black space, tethered to a small ship.
core.cn: 核心意象：白色宇航服的水手漂浮在漆黑太空里，系着一艘小飞船。

branches.en: SPACEFLIGHT: the trained person and their role on a mission crew.
branches.cn: 航天：受训上太空的人及其在任务乘组中的角色。

branches.en: NAMING AND CAREER: national titles like cosmonaut, and spaceflight as a profession.
branches.cn: 称谓与职业：cosmonaut 等各国称谓，以及航天飞行这门职业。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE AND PLAYFUL: anyone who feels space-like or dresses the part.
branches.cn: 比喻与童趣：任何感觉像在太空或穿上太空装的人。

branches.en: HISTORY: the pioneer astronauts remembered by name.
branches.cn: 历史：被记住名字的先驱宇航员。

branches.en: TRAINING: candidates selected but not yet flown.
branches.cn: 训练：已入选但尚未上天的候选人。

intro.en: astronaut is built on Greek astro- (star) and -naut (sailor); the -naut tail also appears in aeronaut, cosmonaut and aquanaut.
intro.cn: astronaut 由希腊语 astro-（星）和 -naut（水手）构成；-naut 尾还出现在 aeronaut、cosmonaut、aquanaut 中。

latinIntro.en: astro- comes from Greek astron; -naut from Greek nautes. Latin passed both shapes into modern scientific coinages.
latinIntro.cn: astro- 来自希腊 astron；-naut 来自希腊 nautes。这两个词形经由现代科学造词沿用至今。

items.meaning: law of the stars; the science

definition_zh: 天文学家
definition_en: a scientist who studies the universe, stars, planets and other celestial bodies
core_image: 一个戴着眼镜、头发花白的老头站在大型望远镜前，抬头望天
scene: 纪录片里解说员说：Edwin Hubble, the astronomer after whom the great telescope was named, proved the universe is expanding.
sceneCN: 这里指「职业是研究天体的科学家」（第1个义项：专业天文学家）；句意为哈勃望远镜命名的那位天文学家证明了宇宙在膨胀。

senses.title: Professional working in the field
senses.definition: a scientist with advanced training in astronomy, employed by observatories, universities or space agencies
senses.definitionCN: 受过高等天文学训练，被天文台、大学或航天机构雇佣的科学家
senses.example: The astronomer stayed up all night collecting data on a rare comet.
senses.exampleCN: 那位天文学家熬夜收集一颗罕见彗星的数据。
senses.why: Like other -er professions, astronomer names the person who does astronomy.
senses.whyCN: 和其他 -er 职业一样，astronomer 就是做 astronomy 的人。

senses.title: Amateur astronomer
senses.definition: a person who observes the sky as a hobby, often with modest equipment but serious enthusiasm
senses.definitionCN: 以观星为爱好的人，设备可能不高级但热情很高
senses.example: An amateur astronomer in Australia spotted a new asteroid before any professional.
senses.exampleCN: 一位澳大利亚业余天文学家比任何职业的都早发现了一颗新小行星。
senses.why: Amateur astronomers can out-professionals when the sky is dark and the target is faint.
senses.whyCN: 业余天文学家能超过职业的，特别是在天空漆黑、目标又暗的时候。

senses.title: Observational vs theoretical
senses.definition: subspecialties: observational astronomers collect data; theoretical astronomers build models
senses.definitionCN: 子专业：观测天文学家收集数据，理论天文学家建立模型
senses.example: She is an observational astronomer who specialises in measuring exoplanet sizes.
senses.exampleCN: 她是专门测量系外行星大小的观测天文学家。
senses.why: Astronomy has the classic split between those who gather evidence and those who explain it.
senses.whyCN: 天文学有经典的分工：收集证据的人和解释证据的人。

senses.title: Historic astronomers
senses.definition: people across cultures who studied the sky before modern science, including Copernicus, Galileo, Kepler, Tycho Brahe
senses.definitionCN: 现代科学之前研究天空的跨文化人物，如哥白尼、伽利略、开普勒、第谷
senses.example: Ancient Arab astronomers gave us most of the star names we still use today.
senses.exampleCN: 古代阿拉伯天文学家给了我们今天仍在使用的大部分星名。
senses.why: Historic astronomers are part of the long tradition that modern astronomy builds on.
senses.whyCN: 历史天文学家是现代天文学所依赖的悠久传统的一部分。

senses.title: Astronomer vs astrophysicist
senses.titleCN: 天文学家 vs 天体物理学家
senses.definition: the boundaries blur; astrophysicists study the physics of celestial objects, astronomers can work in observation or theory broadly
senses.definitionCN: 边界模糊：天体物理学家研究天体物理；天文学家可广泛做观测或理论
senses.example: Many astronomers today are also astrophysicists — the overlap is large.
senses.exampleCN: 今天许多天文学家也是天体物理学家——重叠很大。
senses.why: Both -ist professions share the astron- root, but astrophysicists explicitly study the 'physics' part.
senses.whyCN: 两种 -ist 职业共享 astron- 词根，但 astrophysicist 明确研究 physics 那部分。

senses.title: Astronomer as public scientist
senses.titleCN: 作为公共科学家的天文学家
senses.definition: many astronomers are active science communicators, appearing in documentaries and public talks
senses.definitionCN: 许多天文学家是活跃的科学传播者，出现在纪录片和公共演讲里
senses.example: The astronomer is a regular on late-night science shows.
senses.exampleCN: 这位天文学家是深夜科学节目的常客。
senses.why: Astronomy has broad public appeal — everyone looks up — so astronomers are often the face of science.
senses.whyCN: 天文学有广泛公众吸引力——人人抬头看——所以天文学家常成为科学的脸面。

senses.title: Astronomer at a research facility
senses.titleCN: 科研机构里的天文学家
senses.definition: a staff member of an observatory, space agency or research institute, handling data across projects
senses.definitionCN: 天文台、航天机构或研究所的职员，处理跨项目的数据
senses.example: The observatory employs 12 astronomers to run its flagship telescope.
senses.exampleCN: 这座天文台雇了 12 位天文学家运营它的旗舰望远镜。
senses.why: Big science requires teams, so astronomers work as staff rather than as lone geniuses.
senses.whyCN: 大科学需要团队，所以天文学家是作为职员工作，不是独行天才。

senses.title: Children / dreamers using the word
senses.definition: used informally for anyone fascinated by the sky, not just qualified scientists
senses.definitionCN: 非正式地指任何对天空着迷的人，不只合格科学家
senses.example: As a child I wanted to be an astronomer; now I just look up from the balcony.
senses.exampleCN: 小时候我想当天文学家；现在就从阳台上抬头看看。
senses.why: The word carries wonder, so it's used by dreamers as well as by specialists.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带着浪漫感，所以梦想家和专业人士都用。

intro.en: astronomer adds the English -er agent suffix to astronomy, which itself comes from Greek astron (star) + nomos (law).
intro.cn: astronomer 在 astronomy 上加英语 -er 施事后缀；astronomy 本身来自希腊 astron（星）+ nomos（法）。

items.en: Greek astronomos meant 'one versed in the laws of stars'.
items.cn: 希腊语 astronomos 意为「精通星辰之法的人」。

items.en: Latin astronomus was borrowed directly, meaning 'an astronomer'.
items.cn: 拉丁语直接借入 astronomus，意为「天文学家」。

items.en: Middle English astronomer (14th century) came via Old French astronomier.
items.cn: 中古英语 astronomer（14 世纪）经古法语 astronomier 而来。

items.en: The spelling settled to astronomer, matching astronom- + -er.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 astronomer，对齐 astronom- + -er。

items.en: As astronomy split into subfields, astronomer kept its broad sense while astrophysicist and cosmologist became narrower terms.
items.cn: 当 astronomy 分成子学科时，astronomer 保持广义，而 astrophysicist 和 cosmologist 变得更窄。

items.en: Professional, amateur, historic and popular senses all remain active.
items.cn: 职业、业余、历史、大众的义项今天都仍在使用。

note.en: Group one shares the astron- root with -er / -ist professions; group two are other celestial professionals.
note.cn: 第一组共享 astron- 词根的 -er / -ist 职业；第二组是其他天体领域的专业人士。

entries.definition: General term for someone who studies the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指研究天空的人。

entries.definition: Someone who studies the physics of celestial bodies; subset of astronomer.
entries.definitionCN: 研究天体物理的人；astronomer 的子集。

entries.definition: Astronomer who studies the origin and structure of the whole universe.
entries.definitionCN: 研究整个宇宙起源和结构的天文学家。

entries.definition: Studies life in the universe; not strictly an astronomer.
entries.definitionCN: 研究宇宙中的生命；严格说不算 astronomer。

entries.definition: Flies spacecraft; not a scientist, though many have astronomy backgrounds.
entries.definitionCN: 驾驶航天器的；不是科学家，虽然很多有天文背景。

entries.definition: Uses celestial positions for divination; not a scientist.
entries.definitionCN: 用天体位置占卜；不是科学家。

entries.definition: Bigger category including astronomers, planetary scientists, etc.
entries.definitionCN: 更大的类别，包括天文学家、行星科学家等。

entries.definition: Often an astronomer by training who manages the facility.
entries.definitionCN: 通常是训练有素的天文学家，同时管理天文台。

normalIntro.en: An astronomer is someone who does astronomy.
normalIntro.cn: An astronomer 就是做 astronomy 的人。

normal.en: astronomy + -er = astronomer, just like teacher = teach + -er.
normal.cn: astronomy + -er = astronomer，就像 teacher = teach + -er。

normal.en: Astronomers use telescopes; astrologers use horoscopes.
normal.cn: Astronomers 用望远镜；astrologers 用星盘。

normal.en: Amateur astronomers find comets too — you don't need a PhD.
normal.cn: 业余天文学家也能发现彗星——不一定要博士。

normal.en: Edwin Hubble is the astronomer after whom the telescope is named.
normal.cn: Edwin Hubble 就是哈勃望远镜名字的那位 astronomer。

normal.en: The astronomer stays up all night because the sky is darkest then.
normal.cn: 天文学家熬夜因为那时天空最黑。

abstract.en: A single person in the dark, looking up through glass at light that left a star before the Earth was born.
abstract.cn: 黑暗中的一个人，透过玻璃看着早在地球诞生前就离开恒星的光。

abstract.en: A notebook full of numbers, a red headlamp, cold coffee at 3am.
abstract.cn: 一本写满数字的笔记本、红色头灯、凌晨三点的冷咖啡。

abstract.en: Tiny, alone, and looking upward out of sheer habit.
abstract.cn: 微小、孤独、纯粹出于习惯地向上看。

examples.en: The astronomer's paper on black hole imaging won the biggest prize in physics that year.

examples.en: My cousin is an amateur astronomer who drives to the desert every new moon.
examples.cn: 我表弟是业余天文学家，每个新月都开车去沙漠。

examples.en: Astronomers from 20 nations collaborated to build the Event Horizon Telescope.

definition_zh: 天文学的；天文数字的
definition_en: relating to astronomy; (informal) extremely large
core_image: 哈勃望远镜拍摄的深空照片——密密麻麻的星系像撒了一把糖
scene: 新闻里解说员说：The new fusion plant will require an astronomical investment before it can produce a single watt.
sceneCN: 这里指「数量极其巨大的」（第2个义项：非正式，表示天文数字）；句意为这座新聚变电站要投入天文数字的钱才能产生一瓦电。

pos.zh: 天文学的；（口语）天文数字的

senses.title: Relating to the science of astronomy
senses.definition: the core technical sense: of, belonging to, or using methods of astronomy
senses.definitionCN: 核心技术义项：属于天文学的、使用天文学方法的
senses.example: The observatory was built for astronomical observations of the southern sky.
senses.exampleCN: 这座天文台是为南半球的天文观测而建的。
senses.why: This is the literal adjective: anything connected to astronomy is astronomical.
senses.whyCN: 这就是字面形容词：跟 astronomy 有关的就是 astronomical。

senses.title: Extremely large or huge
senses.definition: informal usage: so large it dwarfs normal human-scale numbers, like distances in space
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法：大到超过人类日常数字尺度，像宇宙里的距离那样
senses.example: The stadium renovation cost an astronomical sum of money.
senses.exampleCN: 体育场改造花了天文数字的钱。
senses.why: Astronomical numbers are the distances and sizes we talk about in astronomy: light-years, billions of stars.
senses.whyCN: 天文数字就是 astronomy 里用的距离和大小：光年、几十亿颗星。

senses.title: Astronomical instruments and methods
senses.definition: equipment and techniques used to observe or calculate celestial positions and movements
senses.definitionCN: 用于观测或计算天体位置和运动的设备与方法
senses.example: Ancient astronomers used simple astronomical instruments like the astrolabe.
senses.exampleCN: 古代天文学家使用星盘这类简单天文仪器。
senses.why: The adjective applies to the tools that let us do astronomy, not just the subject itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也用于做 astronomy 的工具，不只是主题本身。

senses.title: Astronomical scale of the universe
senses.definition: the unimaginable scale of time, distance and energy that astronomy deals with
senses.definitionCN: astronomy 涉及的时间、距离、能量的难以想象的尺度
senses.example: The expansion of the universe happens on astronomical timescales — billions of years.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙膨胀发生在天文尺度的时间上——几十亿年。
senses.why: In science, astronomical often reminds us that we are dealing with numbers beyond everyday experience.
senses.whyCN: 科学里 astronomical 常提醒我们正在处理超出日常经验的数字。

senses.title: Historic astronomical events
senses.definition: events visible to the naked eye — eclipses, comets, supernovae — recorded across cultures and centuries
senses.definitionCN: 肉眼可见的天文事件——日食、彗星、超新星——在各种文化和世纪中被记录
senses.example: The 1882 transit of Venus was an astronomical event observed across the globe.
senses.exampleCN: 1882 年金星凌日是一场全球观测的天文事件。
senses.why: Historic astronomical events bring the science out of the observatory and into public memory.
senses.whyCN: 历史天文事件把科学从天文台带进了公众记忆。

senses.title: Astronomical observations today
senses.definition: data collected by modern ground-based and space telescopes across the electromagnetic spectrum
senses.definitionCN: 现代地面和太空望远镜在整个电磁波谱上收集的数据
senses.example: Astronomical observations from Hubble transformed our view of galaxy formation.
senses.exampleCN: 哈勃的天文观测改变了我们对星系形成的看法。
senses.why: Observations remain the foundation of astronomical knowledge, even as theory grows.
senses.whyCN: 观测始终是天文知识的基础，哪怕理论在长大。

senses.title: Astronomical vs astrological
senses.titleCN: 天文的 vs 占星的
senses.definition: astronomical means scientific; astrological means interpreting human affairs from celestial positions
senses.definitionCN: astronomical 指科学的；astrological 指用天体位置解读人类事务的
senses.example: Astronomical charts differ fundamentally from astrological horoscopes.
senses.exampleCN: 天文图和占星星盘有根本区别。
senses.why: The distinction matters because both use the sky, but only one is a science.
senses.whyCN: 这个区分重要，因为两者都看天空但只有一个是科学。

senses.title: Astronomical investment in research
senses.titleCN: 天文级规模的科研投入
senses.definition: large international partnerships building observatories that cost billions of dollars over decades
senses.definitionCN: 耗资数十亿、历时数十年的大型国际联合天文台
senses.example: The James Webb Space Telescope was an astronomical investment spanning 25 years and many nations.
senses.exampleCN: 韦伯太空望远镜是跨越 25 年、多国参与的天文级投资。
senses.why: Big science on a cosmic scale requires budgets that seem astronomical themselves.
senses.whyCN: 宇宙尺度上的大科学需要的预算本身也显得很 astronomical。

intro.en: astronomical is a Greek-derived adjective: astron (star) + nomos (law) + -ical (adjective suffix), meaning 'pertaining to the law of stars'.
intro.cn: astronomical 是希腊来源的形容词：astron（星）+ nomos（法）+ -ical（形容词后缀），意为「与星辰之法有关的」。

items.en: astronomikos existed in Greek, from astronomia 'law of stars'.
items.cn: 希腊语已有 astronomikos，来自 astronomia「星辰之法」。

items.en: Latin borrowed astronomicus as a direct calque.
items.cn: 拉丁语直接借入 astronomicus。

items.en: Middle English astronomik appeared in the 14th century.
items.cn: 中古英语 astronomik 在 14 世纪出现。

items.en: astronomical appeared alongside astronomy in the 16th century.
items.cn: astronomical 与 astronomy 一起在 16 世纪出现。

items.en: The 'extremely large' sense developed in the 18th century, from the scale of numbers in astronomy.
items.cn: 18 世纪发展出「极大的」含义，来自 astronomy 里数字的尺度。

items.en: Both the scientific and the informal 'huge' sense are common.
items.cn: 科学义项和口语「极大的」义项今天都常用。

note.en: Group one shares the astronom- root; group two collects 'very large' synonyms and other 'astron-' adjectives.

entries.definition: Someone who works with astronomical data.

entries.definition: Of or relating to astrophysics — physics of celestial bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 与天体物理有关的。

entries.definition: Of spacecraft and space travel, not of stars themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 关于航天器和航天的，不是关于恒星本身的。

entries.definitionCN: 用于巨大的物理事物，如山或雕像。

entries.definition: Relating to the whole universe; often used figuratively for immense scale.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个宇宙有关的；常比喻极大尺度。

entries.definitionCN: 关于星系的；有时比喻巨大数额。

entries.definition: Used to intensify size or distance in scientific writing.

normalIntro.en: astronomical = of the stars; stars are far and big → astronomical = huge.
normalIntro.cn: astronomical = 星辰的；星辰远又大 → astronomical = 极大的。

normal.en: astron- = star + -nomical = following law → astronomical.
normal.cn: astron- = 星 + -nomical = 遵法 → astronomical。

normal.en: Stars are astronomical in both their science and their distance.
normal.cn: 星辰在科学上和尺度上都是 astronomical。

normal.en: An astronomical number is a number as big as distances between stars.
normal.cn: astronomical 数字就是像恒星间距离那么大的数字。

normal.en: The Hubble telescope makes astronomical observations.
normal.cn: 哈勃望远镜做 astronomical 观测。

normal.en: Astronomical budgets fund projects on the scale of the universe.
normal.cn: Astronomical 规模的预算资助宇宙尺度的项目。

abstract.en: A number written with so many zeros it fades off the page like stars into space.
abstract.cn: 一个写着太多零、像星星一样淡出纸边的数字。

abstract.en: Looking up from a telescope into a sky with no bottom.
abstract.cn: 从望远镜里望向无边无际的夜空。

abstract.en: A small coin held up against an enormous galaxy.
abstract.cn: 一枚小硬币贴在一个巨大的星系图前。

examples.en: The festival featured talks from leading astronomers and live astronomical observations.
examples.cn: 节庆有顶尖天文学家的报告和实时天文观测。

examples.en: The country's national debt reached astronomical proportions.
examples.cn: 这个国家的国债达到了天文数字。

examples.en: Astronomical spectroscopy can tell us what a distant star is made of.
examples.cn: 天文光谱学能告诉我们一颗遥远恒星由什么构成。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a galaxy image from Hubble, thousands of points of light on a black background, incomprehensibly far.
core.cn: 核心意象：哈勃拍的星系图，黑底上几千个光点，远得难以想象。

branches.cn: 仪器与观测：用来观测天空的设备、方法与数据。

latinIntro.en: astr- is Greek; Latin 'star' is stella, which gives stellar.
latinIntro.cn: astr- 来自希腊语；拉丁语的「星」是 stella，给出 stellar。

definition_zh: 天文学
definition_en: the scientific study of the universe, stars, planets and other celestial bodies
core_image: 一张从地球轨道向外看去的银河全景图，星点密密麻麻
scene: 开学第一节课老师说：Astronomy asks what the universe is made of, how it began, and where it's going.
sceneCN: 这里指「研究宇宙和天体的科学」（第1个义项：科学学科）；句意为天文学追问宇宙由什么构成、如何起源、去往何处。

senses.title: The scientific discipline itself
senses.titleCN: 作为学科本身的天文学
senses.definition: one of the oldest natural sciences, studying everything outside Earth's atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 最古老的自然科学之一，研究地球大气层以外的一切
senses.example: Astronomy has reshaped our picture of the universe in the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 过去一百年里天文学重塑了我们对宇宙的认识。
senses.why: The Greek roots astron (star) + nomos (law) make this the 'law of stars'.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 astron（星）+ nomos（法）让它成为「星辰之法」。

senses.title: Observational astronomy
senses.definition: the branch that gathers data with telescopes, cameras and detectors from the ground or space
senses.definitionCN: 用望远镜、相机和探测器从地面或太空收集数据的分支
senses.example: Observational astronomy got a new eye when the Hubble telescope launched in 1990.
senses.exampleCN: 1990 年哈勃升空给观测天文学添了一只新眼。
senses.why: Observational astronomy is the empirical side, gathering evidence that theorists use.
senses.whyCN: 观测天文学是经验的一面，收集理论家使用的证据。

senses.title: Theoretical astronomy
senses.definition: the branch that builds models to explain what observations reveal
senses.definitionCN: 建立模型解释观测结果的分支
senses.example: Theoretical astronomy predicts where black holes should lie in galaxy centres.
senses.exampleCN: 理论天文学预言黑洞应该在星系中心哪里。
senses.why: Theory gives meaning to observations, turning data into understanding.
senses.whyCN: 理论给观测赋予意义，把数据变成理解。

senses.title: Astronomy history and pre-scientific
senses.titleCN: 前科学的天文观测（历史上）
senses.definition: the ancient practice of tracking skies for calendars, religion or navigation, before the scientific method
senses.definitionCN: 科学方法出现之前，为历算、宗教或导航追踪天象的古老实践
senses.example: Maya astronomy predicted eclipses with remarkable accuracy without telescopes.
senses.exampleCN: 玛雅天文学不用望远镜就以惊人准确度预测了日食月食。
senses.why: Early astronomy blended with astrology, religion and agriculture.
senses.whyCN: 早期天文学与占星、宗教、农业混在一起。

senses.title: Popular astronomy / stargazing
senses.definition: the hobby or public outreach of observing the sky with small telescopes or the naked eye
senses.definitionCN: 用小望远镜或肉眼观星的爱好或科普活动
senses.example: The park hosts free astronomy nights every month for the public.
senses.exampleCN: 公园每月给公众办免费天文之夜。
senses.why: Popular astronomy shares the sky with non-scientists, keeping wonder alive.
senses.whyCN: 科普天文把星空分享给非科学家，让好奇心延续。

senses.title: Subfields: planetary, stellar, galactic
senses.definition: astronomy splits into subfields by object studied: planets, stars, galaxies, the universe as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 按研究对象划分的子学科：行星、恒星、星系、宇宙整体
senses.example: She chose galactic astronomy, studying how the Milky Way formed.
senses.exampleCN: 她选了星系天文学，研究银河系如何形成。
senses.why: Each subfield brings its own tools and questions, but all belong under the same root.
senses.whyCN: 每个子学科有自己的工具和问题，但都在同一词根之下。

senses.title: Astrology vs astronomy
senses.definition: astronomy is the scientific study; astrology uses celestial positions to predict human affairs and is not a science
senses.definitionCN: astronomy 是科学研究；占星用天体位置预言人类事务，不是科学
senses.example: Most universities offer astronomy, none offer astrology as a science.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数大学教 astronomy，没有哪所大学把占星作为科学开设。
senses.why: The -logy ending in astrology sounds scientific but does not mean it uses the scientific method.
senses.whyCN: astrology 里的 -logy 听起来科学但不代表它用科学方法。

senses.title: Influencing other sciences
senses.definition: astronomy overlaps with physics, chemistry, geology, biology and information science
senses.definitionCN: astronomy 与物理、化学、地质、生物、信息科学有交叉
senses.example: Discoveries in astronomy often drive new inventions in sensing and computing.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学的发现常常推动传感和计算的新发明。
senses.why: The universe is the largest laboratory; everything physical here is also physical 'out there'.
senses.whyCN: 宇宙是最大的实验室；这里一切物理事物在「外面」也是物理的。

intro.en: astronomy comes from Greek: astron 'star' + nomos 'law, custom' → 'the law of stars'; it arrived in Latin as astronomia and entered English around the 13th century.
intro.cn: astronomy 来自希腊语：astron「星」+ nomos「法」→「星辰之法」；经拉丁语 astronomia，13 世纪进入英语。

items.en: Aristotle used astronomia to mean the study of celestial motions; nomos meant 'the law that governs'.
items.cn: 亚里士多德用 astronomia 指对天体运动的研究；nomos 意为「支配之法」。

items.en: Latin borrowed astronomia directly from Greek, keeping both the word and the meaning.
items.cn: 拉丁语直接从希腊语借入 astronomia，词和意思都不变。

items.en: Middle English astronomie (13th century) was the standard spelling, borrowed through Old French astronomie.
items.cn: 中古英语 astronomie（13 世纪）是标准拼写，经古法语 astronomie 借入。

items.en: Spelling shifted to astronomy by the 16th century, matching the Greek -nomy suffix pattern.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪拼写变成 astronomy，对齐希腊 -nomy 后缀形式。

items.en: Copernicus and Kepler redefined astronomy in the 16th and 17th centuries as mathematical physics of the heavens.
items.cn: 哥白尼和开普勒在 16-17 世纪把 astronomy 重新定义为天上的数学物理。

items.en: Today astronomy spans from subatomic particles to the structure of the cosmos.
items.cn: 今天 astronomy 从亚原子粒子延伸到宇宙结构。

note.en: Group one holds astronomy-derived words; group two holds related 'sky science' and related -nomy / -logy terms.
note.cn: 第一组是 astronomy 派生的词；第二组是相关的「天空科学」和相近的 -nomy / -logy 术语。

entries.definition: A person who works in astronomy.
entries.definitionCN: 做 astronomy 的人。

entries.definition: Of astronomy; informally, huge in size.
entries.definitionCN: 天文学的；口语里表示「极大的」。

entries.definition: Physics applied to astronomical objects; technically a subfield.
entries.definitionCN: 用物理研究天体；严格说是 astronomy 的子学科。

entries.definition: The study of life in the universe; also called exobiology.
entries.definitionCN: 研究宇宙中的生命；也叫 exobiology。

entries.definition: Not a science; uses celestial positions to interpret human affairs.
entries.definitionCN: 非科学；用天体位置解读人类事务。

entries.definition: The part of astronomy that studies the origin and structure of the whole universe.
entries.definitionCN: 研究整个宇宙起源和结构的 astronomy 分支。

entries.definition: The specific study of how the universe began; narrower than cosmology.
entries.definitionCN: 专门研究宇宙如何起源；范围比 cosmology 窄。

entries.definition: Describing and mapping the universe rather than modelling its physics.
entries.definitionCN: 描述和绘制宇宙，而非建模其物理。

normalIntro.cn: astron- = 星，-nomy = 法 → astronomy = 星辰之法。

normal.cn: astron（希腊语「星」）+ nomos（希腊语「法」）= astronomy。

abstract.en: A clear night, the Milky Way overhead, a telescope pointing somewhere deep.
abstract.cn: 晴朗的夜，头顶银河，望远镜指向深处某处。

abstract.en: A thousand-year quest to figure out where we are and why.
abstract.cn: 一场绵延千年的追问：我们在哪、为什么。

abstract.en: Something ancient, vast, and always pointing up.
abstract.cn: 一种古老、浩瀚、永远向上指的东西。

examples.cn: 射电天文学始于 1930 年代，工程师无意中接收到宇宙射电噪声。

examples.en: Astronomy is a team science; modern observations involve telescopes on every continent and in space.
examples.cn: astronomy 是团队科学；现代观测涉及每个大陆和太空的望远镜。

examples.en: Her PhD combined astronomy with statistics to hunt for exoplanets.
examples.cn: 她的博士结合了天文学和统计来寻找系外行星。

root: astron（希腊语，星）+ nomos（法）→ astronomia → astronomy。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses map the many ways we study the sky: observing, theorising, history, popular enthusiasm, subfields, distinguishing from astrology, and influence on other sciences.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项覆盖我们研究天空的种种方式：观测、理论、历史、业余爱好、子学科、与占星区分、对其他科学的影响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a telescope pointed at a dark sky, pulling faint stars into bright focus.
core.cn: 核心意象：指向暗空的望远镜，把暗淡的星辰拉成清晰的焦点。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE AND OBSERVATION: the field itself, plus the work of watching and measuring the sky.
branches.cn: 学科与观测：这门学科本身，以及观测测量天空的工作。

branches.en: THEORETICAL: the branch that builds models and predictions.
branches.cn: 理论：负责建立模型与预言的分支。

branches.en: HISTORICAL: pre-scientific sky watching and its records.
branches.cn: 历史：前科学时期的天象观测及其记录。

branches.en: POPULAR / OUTREACH: amateur stargazing and public explanation.
branches.cn: 科普 / 业余：业余观星与面向公众的解释。

branches.en: CLASSIFICATION / BOUNDARIES / INFLUENCE: subfields, the line against astrology, and effects on other sciences.
branches.cn: 分类 / 边界 / 影响：子学科、与占星的界线，以及对其他学科的影响。

intro.en: astronomy is built from Greek astron 'star' plus the Greek suffix -nomy 'law, system of rules'; many astronomy words share astron-.
intro.cn: astronomy 由希腊 astron「星」加希腊后缀 -nomy「法、规则体系」构成；许多 astronomy 相关词都共享 astron-。

latinIntro.en: astron is purely Greek, not Latin; the Latin 'star' is stella, which gives stellar.
latinIntro.cn: astron 纯粹来自希腊，不是拉丁语；拉丁语的「星」是 stella，给出 stellar。

items.meaning: study of the laws of stars
one who navigates among the stars

definition_zh: adj. 不对称的（两侧形状不同）；（关系、信息、力量）不对等的
definition_en: Having two halves that differ in shape or size; of a relationship, unevenly balanced in information, power or obligation.
core_image: 一件衣服左右两片长短不一，天平一头明显下沉
scene: 这件外套左右长短不同，是刻意剪成这样的。The coat has an asymmetric cut, longer on one side.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：asymmetric 指两侧形状或大小不同，即不对称。

senses.title: Unequal in shape
senses.definition: having sides or halves that do not match in shape, size or placement
senses.definitionCN: 两侧或两半在形状、大小或位置上不相配
senses.example: The facade is deliberately asymmetric.
senses.exampleCN: 这个立面是故意做成不对称的。
senses.why: The root means measure, and the prefix removes it, so the word says the two sides cannot be measured alike.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「量度」，前缀把它取消，所以这个词说的是两侧无法用同一尺度量出相同结果。

senses.title: Unequal in a relationship
senses.definition: of information, power or duty, distributed unevenly between the parties involved
senses.definitionCN: 指信息、权力或义务在各方之间分布不均
senses.example: The market fails when information is asymmetric.
senses.exampleCN: 信息不对称时市场就会失灵。
senses.why: Economics borrowed the shape word for balance, because a lopsided scale is the oldest picture of unfairness.
senses.whyCN: 经济学借用了这个形状词来讲「均衡」，因为一头下沉的天平是关于不公最古老的画面。

intro.en: Asymmetric is Greek asymmetros, from a-, without, and symmetria, from syn-, together, and metron, measure: not measuring together.
intro.cn: asymmetric 就是希腊语 asymmetros，由 a-「无」与 symmetria 构成，后者出自 syn-「共同」加 metron「量度」：不能共同量出同一结果。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to measure lies behind metre, measure and geometry alike.
items.cn: 一个意为「量」的拟构词根同时藏在 metre、measure 与 geometry 背后。

items.en: Greek metron meant a measure or a rule for measuring, the core of the whole family.
items.cn: 希腊语 metron 意为「量度、量尺」，是整个词族的核心。

items.en: With syn-, together, symmetria meant measuring together, hence proportion and balanced form.
items.cn: 加上 syn-「共同」后，symmetria 意为「共同量度」，因而指比例与匀称。

items.en: The prefix a- negated it, giving asymmetros, without common measure.
items.cn: 前缀 a- 加以否定，得到 asymmetros「没有共同量度」。

items.en: English formed asymmetric in the eighteenth century as geometry and design demanded the term.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪构成 asymmetric，因为几何与设计需要这个术语。

items.en: Twentieth-century economics and strategy applied it to information and power, giving the second sense.
items.cn: 二十世纪经济学与战略学把它用于信息与权力，产生第二个义项。

note.en: The look-alike group is the whole measure family with and without the negative prefix; the near-meaning group lists everyday words for lopsidedness.
note.cn: 形近组是带与不带否定前缀的整个「量度」词族；近义组列出日常表示「一边偏」的词。

entries.definition: Having matching halves.
entries.definitionCN: 两半相配的。

entries.definition: The absence of symmetry.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏对称。

entries.definition: Relating to shapes and their measures.
entries.definitionCN: 与形状及其量度有关的。

entries.definition: Relating to measurement or a system of it.
entries.definitionCN: 与测量或度量制有关的。

entries.definition: Heavier or lower on one side.
entries.definitionCN: 一侧更重或更低。

entries.definition: Not level, smooth or balanced.
entries.definitionCN: 不平、不匀或不均衡。

entries.definition: Lacking equal weight or stability.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏均等的分量或稳定。

entries.definition: Favouring one side only.
entries.definitionCN: 只偏向一方。

normalIntro.en: Asymmetric is a-, not, plus sym-, together, plus metric, measure: the two sides do not measure the same.
normalIntro.cn: asymmetric 就是 a-「不」加 sym-「共同」加 metric「量度」：两侧量不出同一个结果。

normal.en: Asymmetric and asymmetrical are both correct.
normal.cn: asymmetric 与 asymmetrical 都对。

normal.en: Asymmetry is the noun, asymmetrically the adverb.
normal.cn: asymmetry 是名词，asymmetrically 是副词。

normal.en: Symmetric is the same word without the negative.
normal.cn: symmetric 就是去掉否定的同一个词。

normal.en: Asymmetric information is a set economics phrase.
normal.cn: asymmetric information 是经济学固定说法。

normal.en: Lopsided is the everyday substitute.
normal.cn: lopsided 是日常替换词。

abstract.en: Picture a coat longer on the left than the right.
abstract.cn: 想象一件左边比右边长的外套。

abstract.en: Imagine a scale with one pan clearly lower.
abstract.cn: 想象一头明显下沉的天平。

abstract.en: Think of one side knowing what the other cannot.
abstract.cn: 想象一方知道另一方无从知道的事。

examples.en: The garden follows an asymmetric plan.
examples.cn: 这座花园采用不对称的布局。

examples.en: Asymmetric power breeds resentment.
examples.cn: 权力不对等会滋生怨恨。

examples.en: Her smile was slightly asymmetric.
examples.cn: 她的笑略微不对称。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「不」+ sym「共同」+ metric「量度」——两边量不到一块儿，就是不对称 asymmetric。

root: 希腊语 metron「量度」加 syn-「共同」构成 symmetria「匀称」，再加否定前缀 a- 成 asymmetros；英语十八世纪造 asymmetric，二十世纪扩用于信息与权力。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses deny a common measure: two halves that will not match, and two parties who do not hold the same weight.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都否认「共同量度」：无法相配的两半，以及分量不同的两方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one side longer, one pan of the scale clearly lower
core.cn: 核心意象：一件衣服左右两片长短不一，天平一头明显下沉

branches.en: A coat longer on one side.
A facade built off centre.
One pan of the scale lower.
One side knowing more than the other.
branches.cn: 一方比另一方知道得更多。

branches.en: No common measure between the two sides.
branches.cn: 两侧之间没有共同的量度。

intro.en: Asymmetric is a-, not, sym-, together, metr-, measure, and -ic; the same layers build symmetry, geometry and isometric.
intro.cn: asymmetric 由 a-「不」、sym-「共同」、metr-「量度」与 -ic 构成；同样的层次还构成 symmetry、geometry 与 isometric。

latinIntro.en: The classical layer is Greek metron, measure, and symmetria, proportion, matched by Latin mensura and ratio.
latinIntro.cn: 古典层次是希腊语 metron「量度」与 symmetria「比例」，对应拉丁语 mensura 与 ratio。

latinEntries.exampleCN: metrum 产生 metre 与 metric。

definition_zh: 不对称；不对称性；失衡；不平等的分布
definition_en: the absence of exact correspondence between two sides, or a deliberate imbalance between parts
core_image: 一只碗左右两侧厚薄不同，转起来明显偏向一边
scene: 陶艺工作台上，一只碗的左右两侧厚薄不同，转起来明显偏向一边，The potter deliberately preserves the asymmetry of the rim.
sceneCN: 这里 asymmetry 指「两侧缺乏镜像对应的性质」（第 1 个义项：不对称）；句意为陶艺师有意保留碗口的不对称。图中可辨识物件：拉坯工作台、偏厚的碗壁、转盘与刻刀。

senses.title: Absence of mirror correspondence
senses.definition: the state of two sides not matching when folded or compared
senses.definitionCN: 两半在对折或比较时无法吻合的状态
senses.example: The asymmetry of the two wings kept the model from flying straight.
senses.exampleCN: 两翅的不对称让模型无法直线飞行。
senses.why: The negative prefix a- simply denies symmetry, so the core sense is symmetry's mirror test failing.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀直接否定了「对称」，因此核心义就是镜像检验不成立。

senses.title: Deliberate imbalance in composition
senses.titleCN: 构图中刻意安排的失衡
senses.definition: an intentional uneven arrangement used by artists and designers for energy or tension
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家与设计师为制造动势或张力而故意采用的不均等布局
senses.example: The poster's asymmetry pulls the eye toward the lower corner.
senses.exampleCN: 海报的不对称把视线拉向左下角。
senses.why: In art, breaking symmetry is a tool rather than a defect, so the word can name a chosen effect.
senses.whyCN: 在艺术中，打破对称是工具而非缺陷，因此这个词可以指一种刻意营造的效果。

senses.title: Absence of invariance in mathematics
senses.definition: the failure of an object or equation to remain unchanged under a given transformation
senses.definitionCN: 对象或方程在某种变换下无法保持原样
senses.example: The asymmetry of the matrix means the two operations do not commute.
senses.exampleCN: 矩阵的不对称意味着两种运算不可交换。
senses.why: If symmetry is invariance under transformation, asymmetry is the measurable failure of that invariance.
senses.whyCN: 若对称是变换下的不变性，不对称就是这种不变性的可测失效。

senses.title: Unequal development in an organism
senses.definition: a difference in size, shape or position between paired parts of a living body
senses.definitionCN: 生物成对部位在大小、形状或位置上的差异
senses.example: The crab's one enlarged claw is a clear example of asymmetry.
senses.exampleCN: 这只蟹一只钳子特别大，是不对称的明显例子。
senses.why: Body plans can depart from mirror balance, and biology uses the plain geometric word for that departure.
senses.whyCN: 体制可以偏离镜像平衡，生物学便用这个朴素的几何词来指这种偏离。

senses.title: Information asymmetry
senses.definition: a situation in which one party knows more than another, affecting bargaining or fairness
senses.definitionCN: 一方比另一方掌握更多信息、从而影响议价或公平的情形
senses.example: Used-car markets suffer from information asymmetry between seller and buyer.
senses.exampleCN: 二手车市场受制于买卖双方之间的信息不对称。
senses.why: Economics borrows the shape metaphor: the two sides of a transaction do not see the same amount.
senses.whyCN: 经济学借用形状比喻：交易两边看到的信息量并不相同。

senses.title: Matter-antimatter asymmetry
senses.titleCN: 物质与反物质的不对称
senses.definition: the observed imbalance between matter and antimatter in the universe
senses.definitionCN: 宇宙中物质与反物质之间被观测到的不平衡
senses.example: Physicists still explain the universe's matter asymmetry.
senses.exampleCN: 物理学家仍在解释宇宙的物质不对称。
senses.why: Here asymmetry names a difference in quantity between two classes that should, by symmetry, have been equal.
senses.whyCN: 这里的对称缺失指两类本应相等的物质在数量上出现了差异。

senses.title: Unequal size or shape in medicine
senses.titleCN: 医学上的大小或形状不等
senses.definition: a clinical difference between paired structures, such as pupils or limbs
senses.definitionCN: 成对结构（如瞳孔或肢体）在临床上的差异
senses.example: Sudden asymmetry of the pupils can signal a serious problem.
senses.exampleCN: 瞳孔突然不对称可能提示严重问题。
senses.why: Medicine uses the word for any paired structures that no longer match, without judging cause.
senses.whyCN: 医学用这个词指任何不再吻合的成对结构，并不判断成因。

senses.title: General irregularity or lack of harmony
senses.definition: a figurative want of balance or harmony between things
senses.definitionCN: 事物之间比喻意义上的失衡或不协调
senses.example: There is an asymmetry between the team's ambitions and its budget.
senses.exampleCN: 团队的雄心与预算之间存在一种不对等。
senses.why: The geometric word extends to any pair whose two sides carry unequal weight.
senses.whyCN: 这个几何词扩展到任何两边分量不相等的配对。

intro.en: Asymmetry joins Greek a- 'not' to symmetria 'agreement in measure'. The negative form asymmetria existed in Greek, and English adopted the pattern in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: asymmetry 把希腊语否定前缀 a-「不」加到 symmetria「度量一致」上。希腊语已有否定形式 asymmetria，英语在 17 世纪沿用这一构词模式。年代均为约数。

items.en: The prefix a- (the alpha privative) negates the word it attaches to, as in atypical or anonymous.
items.cn: 前缀 a-（否定性的 alpha）否定所附之词，如 atypical 或 anonymous。

items.en: Symmetria meant 'agreement in dimensions, due proportion', from syn- 'together' and metron 'measure'.
items.cn: symmetria 意为「尺寸一致、比例得当」，由 syn-「共同」与 metron「度量」构成。

items.en: The Greeks used asymmetria for want of proportion, chiefly in describing bodies and buildings that did not balance.
items.cn: 希腊人用 asymmetria 指比例失调，主要用于描述不均衡的人体与建筑。

items.en: English formed asymmetry in the seventeenth century, first in geometry and natural philosophy, then in general description.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪构成 asymmetry，先用于几何学与自然哲学，后进入一般描述。

items.en: In the twentieth century economics, particle physics and medicine each gave the word a precise technical application.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，经济学、粒子物理与医学各自赋予这个词精确的技术用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first record and deeper root): the earliest English citation is approximate, and the pre-Greek origin of metron remains unsettled, so proposed roots are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：英语最早书证只是约数，metron 在希腊语之前的来源仍无定论，所提词根属重构形式。

note.en: The first group holds forms built on the same root, plus the positive term they deny; the second holds words for imbalance that are less technical.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词形及其所否定的肯定词；第二组是表示失衡但技术性较弱的词。

entries.definition: The technical adjective meaning lacking symmetry, common in science and engineering.
entries.definitionCN: 表示缺乏对称的技术形容词，常见于科学与工程。

entries.definition: The everyday adjective with the same meaning; the choice between the two is stylistic, not semantic.
entries.definitionCN: 同义的日常形容词；二者之别在文体，不在词义。

entries.definition: The positive noun that asymmetry negates; it is not a look-alike but the exact opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 被 asymmetry 否定的肯定名词；不是形近词，而是精确的反义。

entries.definition: A lack of even distribution, often of weight, power or resources; it carries no geometric image.
entries.definitionCN: 分布不均，常指重量、权力或资源；不带几何形象。

entries.definition: A failure of parts to be rightly proportioned to one another.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分之间未能恰当相称。

entries.definition: A departure from a regular pattern; it is broader and does not imply two comparable sides.
entries.definitionCN: 对规则图案的偏离；更宽泛，且不暗示两个可比的面。

entries.definition: A plain everyday word for one side being heavier or larger than the other.
entries.definitionCN: 日常口语词，指一边比另一边更重或更大。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the negative prefix, the two Greek pieces and the technical uses that make the word precise.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：否定前缀、两个希腊构件，以及使词义精确的技术用法。

normal.en: A- 'not' plus symmetry gives the whole meaning before any example: no matching measure.
normal.cn: 「不」这一否定前缀加「对称」，在任何例子之前就给出了全部含义：没有相同的度量。

normal.en: Fold the paper and the halves miss each other; that miss is the asymmetry.
normal.cn: 把纸对折，两半彼此错过；这一「错过」就是不对称。

normal.en: Artists use asymmetry on purpose, so the word does not always mean a fault.
normal.cn: 艺术家故意使用不对称，所以这个词并不总意味着缺陷。

normal.en: In markets, asymmetry usually means one side knows more than the other.
normal.cn: 在市场里，不对称通常指一方比另一方知道得更多。

normal.en: In physics, the matter asymmetry is a surplus of matter over antimatter.
normal.cn: 在物理学中，物质不对称指物质多于反物质。

abstract.en: Picture a balance scale whose two pans were made to different sizes.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，两只托盘被做成不同大小。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation in which only one speaker can see the notes.
abstract.cn: 想象一场对话，只有一方能看到讲稿。

abstract.en: Picture a face that is almost familiar, with one feature slightly off.
abstract.cn: 想象一张几乎熟悉的脸，只有一个特征略有偏差。

examples.en: The design uses asymmetry to keep the eye moving across the page.
examples.cn: 这个设计用不对称让视线不断扫过页面。

examples.en: Regulators try to reduce information asymmetry between banks and borrowers.
examples.cn: 监管者试图减少银行与借款人之间的信息不对称。

examples.en: The doctor noted a slight asymmetry in the patient's gait.
examples.cn: 医生注意到病人步态略有不对称。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「asymmetry」听成「呃，四面吹里」——四面吹来的风不一样，左右对不上，就是不对称。前面的 a 就是「不」，后面是「度量一致」，合起来就是「度量不一致」。

root: 希腊语否定前缀 a-「不」加 symmetria「度量一致、比例得当」（syn-「共同」+ metron「度量」）构成否定形式 asymmetria；英语在 17 世纪沿用这一模式造出 asymmetry，先用于几何与自然哲学，后进入经济学、物理与医学。metron 的更早来源属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the failure of mirror correspondence, then cover deliberate artistic imbalance, mathematical non-invariance, unequal bodies, information gaps, matter-antimatter imbalance, clinical differences and general disharmony.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从镜像对应失效开始，依次涵盖艺术中的刻意失衡、数学上的非不变性、生物发育不均、信息差、物质与反物质失衡、临床差异与泛指的不协调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet folded along its centre, with the two halves failing to meet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张纸沿中线对折，两半却对不上。

branches.en: THE FAILED TEST: the core sense is two sides that do not match when compared.
branches.cn: 检验失败：核心义是比较时两侧无法吻合。

branches.en: BREAKING AND FAILING: artists break balance on purpose, while mathematics measures a transformation that changes the object.
branches.cn: 打破与失效：艺术家有意打破平衡，数学则衡量使对象改变的变换。

branches.en: UNEQUAL SIDES IN LIFE: paired organs can differ, and two parties can hold unequal information.
branches.cn: 现实中的不等两侧：成对器官可以不同，交易双方也可以掌握不等的信息。

branches.en: QUANTITATIVE AND CLINICAL GAPS: matter outnumbers antimatter, and paired body structures stop matching.
branches.cn: 数量与临床差异：物质多于反物质，成对身体结构也不再吻合。

branches.en: GENERAL DISHARMONY: any pair whose two sides carry unequal weight falls under the widened word.
branches.cn: 泛指不协调：任何两边分量不等的配对都落入这个放宽后的词义。

intro.en: Asymmetry is symmetry with a Greek negative prefix attached, so its parts and derived words are easy to read.
intro.cn: 「不对称」是在「对称」上附加希腊否定前缀而成，构件与派生词都容易读出。

latinIntro.en: Greek a- and symmetria build the noun; Latin carried symmetria, and English added -ic and -ical for the adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 a- 与 symmetria 构成该名词；拉丁承接 symmetria，英语再加两个形容词词尾构成形容词。

items.example: The prefix reverses the meaning of the whole word.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀反转整词含义。

items.example: The prefix survives inside the positive noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀保留在肯定名词内部。

items.example: The root supplies the measuring idea.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「度量」观念。

definition_zh: n. 无神论者（不相信任何神存在的人）；旧指不信正统宗教的人
definition_en: A person who does not believe that any god exists; in older usage, a person who rejected the accepted religion.
core_image: 别人合掌祈祷时，他安静地站着，心里没有那位对象
scene: 他从不参加任何宗教仪式，也这样介绍自己。He describes himself as an atheist.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：atheist 指不相信任何神存在的人，即无神论者。

senses.title: A person who believes in no god
senses.definition: someone who holds that no god exists, a position about belief rather than about knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 主张不存在任何神的人，这是关于「信」而非关于「知」的立场
senses.example: As an atheist he saw no need for a creator.
senses.exampleCN: 作为无神论者，他认为不需要一位造物主。
senses.why: The prefix a- means without and theos means god, so the word states plainly what the person does without.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 a- 意为「无」，theos 意为「神」，所以这个词直白地说出这个人「没有」什么。

senses.title: An older label for rejecting the faith
senses.definition: in earlier writing, a person who denied the accepted gods or religion, often used as an accusation
senses.definitionCN: 在较早文献中指否认公认神祇或宗教的人，常作指控用语
senses.example: The charge of being an atheist once carried real danger.
senses.exampleCN: 被指为无神论者曾带来真实的危险。
senses.why: Because the label was handed out by opponents, the older sense records a social judgement more than a stated belief.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个标签是由对手贴上的，旧义记录的更多是社会评判，而不是本人陈述的信念。

intro.en: Atheist is Greek atheos, from a-, without, and theos, god, through French athee, with the practitioner ending -ist added in English.
intro.cn: atheist 就是希腊语 atheos，由 a-「无」与 theos「神」构成，经法语 athée 传入，英语再加上表示人的后缀 -ist。

items.en: Greek theos meant god, the root of theology, theist and pantheon.
items.cn: 希腊语 theos 意为「神」，是 theology、theist 与 pantheon 的词根。

items.en: With a-, without, atheos meant godless, at first of those who abandoned the city gods.
items.cn: 加上 a-「无」后，atheos 意为「无神的」，起初指背弃城邦诸神的人。

items.en: Greek writers used the word against opponents, so it began as a charge rather than a self-description.
items.cn: 希腊作者用这个词攻击对手，所以它起初是指控，而不是自称。

items.en: French athee carried the word into modern Europe during the religious conflicts.
items.cn: 法语 athée 在宗教冲突时期把这个词带入近代欧洲。

items.en: English added -ist and records atheist from the 1570s, still largely a term of abuse.
items.cn: 英语加上 -ist，从十六世纪七十年代起记录 atheist，当时仍多为贬称。

items.en: From the eighteenth century writers claimed the label openly, turning it into a stated position.
items.cn: 十八世纪起有作者公开认领这个标签，把它变成一种自陈立场。

note.en: The look-alike group sets the opposite and the neighbouring doubt position beside it; the near-meaning group lists other words for unbelief.
note.cn: 形近组把相反立场与邻近的「存疑」立场摆在旁边；近义组列出其他表示不信的词。

entries.definitionCN: 主张公共生活不涉宗教的人。

normalIntro.en: Atheist is a-, without, plus theos, god, plus -ist, a person: someone living without a god.
normalIntro.cn: atheist 就是 a-「无」加 theos「神」再加 -ist「人」：一个生活中没有神的人。

normal.en: Atheism is the position, atheist the person.
normal.cn: atheism 是立场，atheist 是人。

normal.en: Theist is the same word without the negative.

normal.en: Agnostic is about knowing, not believing.

normal.en: Polytheist believes in many gods, monotheist in one.

examples.cn: 无神论作者在那个世纪公开论辩。

root: 希腊语 theos「神」加否定前缀 a- 构成 atheos「无神的」，经法语 athée 入英语并加 -ist 成 atheist；十六世纪多为贬称，十八世纪起成为自陈立场。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses remove a god, but from different hands: one is a person stating a belief, the other a label once thrown by opponents.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都「移走了神」，但出手的人不同：一个是本人陈述信念，另一个是对手曾经贴上的标签。

latinIntro.cn: 古典层次是希腊语 theos「神」，对应拉丁语 deus 与 divinus；否定前缀 a- 也来自希腊语。

definition_en: a person who competes in sport, or a person with a strong trained body
core_image: 跑道起点，一个人压着起跑线
scene: 天还没亮，跑道上已有人在练起跑。The athlete trained for months before the race.
sceneCN: 这里 athlete 是「运动员」（第 1 个义项：参加竞技体育的人）；句意是这名运动员赛前训练了几个月。

pos.zh: 名词：运动员；体格强健的人

derivatives.zh: 形容词：运动的；体格健壮的

senses.title: Competitor in sport
senses.definition: a person who competes in a sport, especially one who trains hard
senses.definitionCN: 参加体育比赛、尤其经过刻苦训练的人
senses.example: The athlete trained for months before the race.
senses.exampleCN: 这名运动员赛前训练了几个月。
senses.why: Athlete comes from Greek athletes, 'one who competes for a prize', built on athlon 'contest or prize', so the word names a contender rather than anyone who exercises.
senses.whyCN: athlete 来自希腊语 athletes「为奖品而竞争的人」，词根 athlon 意为竞赛或奖品，所以它指参赛的竞争者，而不是任何锻炼的人。

senses.title: Strong trained body
senses.definition: a person with a strong, fit and well-trained body
senses.definitionCN: 身材健壮、训练有素的人
senses.example: Her brother is a natural athlete.
senses.exampleCN: 她弟弟天生体格强健。
senses.why: Since contenders are visibly fit, the word stretched from the competitor to anyone built and trained like one.
senses.whyCN: 参赛者通常体格出众，于是这个词从「参赛的人」扩展到「像运动员那样健壮的人」。

intro.en: Athlete is a Greek word for a contender, and its root names the prize itself.
intro.cn: athlete 是希腊语中表示竞争者的人，词根指的正是奖品。

items.en: English athlete named a competitor in games.

items.cn: 这个词也用来形容健壮、训练有素的身体。

normal.en: The adjective is athletic, the field is athletics.

definition_zh: n. 地图集；图谱；（解剖）寰椎，即第一节颈椎
definition_en: A bound collection of maps or charts; in anatomy, the first cervical vertebra, which carries the skull.
core_image: 一个巨人扛着天，一本厚册子扛着整个世界的地图
scene: 他翻开厚厚的地图集去找那条河。He opened the atlas to find the river.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：atlas 指装订成册的地图集，也可指某学科的图谱。

senses.title: A bound book of maps
senses.definition: a collection of maps or charts bound together, and by extension a similar book of plates for any subject
senses.definitionCN: 装订在一起的地图或图表集，引申指任何学科的同类图册
senses.example: The atlas shows every district at the same scale.
senses.exampleCN: 这本地图集用同一比例尺呈现每个区。
senses.why: The name comes from a Titan who held up the sky, so the book is pictured carrying the whole world.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自一位撑住天空的泰坦巨神，于是这本书被想象成扛着整个世界。

senses.title: The vertebra that carries the skull
senses.definition: in anatomy, the topmost vertebra of the neck, named because it bears the head as the Titan bore the sky
senses.definitionCN: 解剖学上指颈部最上一节椎骨，命名因它托着头颅，如巨神托天
senses.example: The atlas allows the head to nod.
senses.exampleCN: 寰椎让头部能上下点头。
senses.why: Anatomists kept the same image of bearing a weight, which is why a bone and a book share one name.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学家沿用了「承重」的同一意象，所以一块骨头与一本书共用一个名字。

intro.en: Atlas is the name of the Greek Titan who held up the sky; Mercator used it as the title of his map collection in 1595, and anatomy borrowed it for the top vertebra.
intro.cn: atlas 是希腊神话中撑天的泰坦巨神之名；1595 年墨卡托用它作自己地图集的标题，解剖学又借它指最上一节椎骨。

items.en: In Greek myth Atlas was a Titan condemned to hold up the heavens at the western edge of the world.
items.cn: 希腊神话中，阿特拉斯是被罚在世界西缘撑住天空的泰坦巨神。

items.en: The sea beyond that edge was named after him, giving Atlantic and Atlantis.
items.cn: 那道边界之外的大洋以他命名，产生 Atlantic 与 Atlantis。

items.en: Builders called supporting male figures atlantes, after the same bearing Titan.
items.cn: 建筑中承重的男性人像柱被称为 atlantes，同样取自这位承重的巨神。

items.en: Mercator titled his collection of maps Atlas, and the title became the common noun for such books.
items.cn: 墨卡托把自己的地图集题为 Atlas，这个标题随后变成此类书的普通名词。

items.en: Anatomists named the first cervical vertebra atlas because it carries the skull.
items.cn: 解剖学家把第一节颈椎命名为 atlas，因为它托着颅骨。

items.en: By the nineteenth century any bound set of plates could be an atlas, from anatomy to clouds.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，任何成册图版都可称 atlas，从解剖到云图皆然。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Titan name into sea and architecture and adds two words that only sound similar; the near-meaning group lists neighbouring reference books.
note.cn: 形近组顺着巨神之名追到海洋与建筑，并加上两个只是音近的词；近义组列出邻近的参考书。

entries.definition: Sculpted male figures used as supports.

entries.definition: A single map or diagram.

normalIntro.en: Atlas is the Titan who carried the sky, so anything that carries a whole world of information takes his name.
normalIntro.cn: atlas 是撑天的泰坦巨神，所以任何承载一整个信息世界的东西都借他的名字。

normal.en: The plural is atlases, not atlasses.

normal.en: An atlas of anything means a bound set of plates.
normal.cn: an atlas of anything 指成册图版。

abstract.en: Imagine a thick book carrying every coastline.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚册子载着每一条海岸线。

abstract.en: Think of one small bone holding up a head.

examples.en: She keeps a road atlas in the car.
examples.cn: 她车里放着一本公路地图册。

examples.en: The scan showed a fracture of the atlas.

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想记忆：巨神 Atlas 扛着天——一本扛着全世界地图的厚册子，就叫 atlas；扛着头的那节颈骨也叫它。

root: 希腊神话中撑天的泰坦 Atlas 之名，先给大西洋与男像柱命名；1595 年墨卡托以 Atlas 题其地图集，十七世纪解剖学又以此称呼托颅的第一颈椎。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses bear a weight: a book carrying the whole world in maps, and a small bone carrying the head.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都在承重：一本书用地图载着整个世界，一块小骨头托着一颗头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a giant holding the sky, a thick book holding the world

branches.en: A thick book of every coastline.

intro.en: Atlas is a proper name turned common noun; its endings build Atlantic, Atlantean and atlantes, while the book sense joins -graphy and -logy.
intro.cn: atlas 是专名转为普通名词；其派生形式有 Atlantic、Atlantean 与 atlantes，而「图册」义则与 -graphy、-logy 组合。

latinIntro.en: The classical layer is the Greek name Atlas, with Latin charta, a sheet of paper, and mappa, a cloth or map, naming the material.
latinIntro.cn: 古典层次是希腊人名 Atlas，另有拉丁语 charta「一张纸」与 mappa「布、地图」指其材质。
