definition_zh: 大气层；空气；气氛
definition_en: the gases around the earth, or the feeling of a place or situation
core_image: 一层薄薄的空气裹着地球
scene: 房间里的笑声忽然停了。The atmosphere in the room turned cold.
sceneCN: 这里 atmosphere 是「气氛」（第 2 个义项：一个场合给人的整体感觉）；句意是屋里的气氛冷了下来。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：大气的；有氛围的
名词：大气干扰；气氛渲染

senses.title: Layer of gases
senses.definition: the mass of gases that surrounds the earth or another planet
senses.definitionCN: 包围地球或其他行星的气体层
senses.example: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 二氧化碳把热量困在大气层里。
senses.why: Atmosphere joins Greek atmos 'vapour' with sphaira 'sphere', so it literally names the ball of vapour wrapped around a planet.
senses.whyCN: atmosphere 把希腊语 atmos「气、蒸气」与 sphaira「球」合在一起，字面就是包在行星外面的一层气球。

senses.title: Feeling of a place
senses.definition: the overall feeling that a place or situation gives people
senses.definitionCN: 一个场合或情境给人的整体感受
senses.example: The atmosphere in the room turned cold.
senses.exampleCN: 屋里的气氛冷了下来。
senses.why: The air that surrounds and fills a room also surrounds a group of people, so the word shifts from the physical gas to the invisible mood that fills a space.
senses.whyCN: 充满房间、包围人的空气，同样包围着一群人；于是这个词从看得见的气体转成充满空间、看不见的情绪。

intro.en: Atmosphere was coined by joining two Greek words for vapour and sphere.
intro.cn: atmosphere 是把两个希腊词「气」与「球」拼起来造出的词。

items.en: atmos meant 'vapour or steam'.
items.cn: atmos 意为「气、蒸气」。

items.en: sphaira meant 'sphere or ball'.
items.cn: sphaira 意为「球体」。

items.en: Scientists coined atmosphere for the vapour around a planet.
items.cn: 科学家造出 atmosphere 一词，指包围行星的气层。

items.en: The word began to describe the mood of a place.
items.cn: 这个词开始用来描述一个场合的气氛。

items.en: Both the climate sense and the mood sense are standard.
items.cn: 大气义与气氛义都已成为标准用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sphere part; the near-meaning group names air and mood.
note.cn: 形近组共享 sphere 部分；近义组是表示空气与情绪的词。

entries.definition: relating to the atmosphere
entries.definitionCN: 大气的

entries.definition: a round solid shape
entries.definitionCN: 球体

entries.definition: half of a sphere
entries.definitionCN: 半球

entries.definition: the gas we breathe
entries.definitionCN: 空气

entries.definition: a temporary feeling
entries.definitionCN: 情绪；氛围

entries.definition: the surrounding conditions
entries.definitionCN: 环境

normalIntro.en: The same word covers the air around a planet and the air of a room.
normalIntro.cn: 同一个词既指行星周围的气层，也指一屋子里的空气。

normal.en: The ph in atmosphere sounds like f.
normal.cn: atmosphere 里的 ph 读作 f。

normal.en: For the gas layer, use the definite article: the atmosphere.
normal.cn: 指大气层时常加定冠词。

normal.en: For mood, use an article: a relaxed atmosphere.
normal.cn: 指气氛时用不定冠词：轻松的气氛。

normal.en: The adjective atmospheric also means full of mood.
normal.cn: 形容词 atmospheric 也可表示「很有氛围的」。

normal.en: The sphere part is the same as in hemisphere.
normal.cn: sphere 这一部分与 hemisphere 相同。

abstract.en: See a thin glowing skin around a blue ball.
abstract.cn: 想象蓝色球体外面一层发光的薄皮。

abstract.en: See a room where nobody speaks after a door shuts.
abstract.cn: 想象门关上后没人说话的屋子。

abstract.en: See breath visible in cold morning air.
abstract.cn: 想象寒冷清晨里可见的呼气。

examples.en: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere.
examples.cn: 二氧化碳把热量困在大气层里。

examples.en: The atmosphere in the room turned cold.
examples.cn: 屋里的气氛冷了下来。

examples.en: The café has a relaxed atmosphere.
examples.cn: 这家咖啡馆气氛轻松。

dict_mnemonic.text: atmos（气）加 sphere（球）：包着星球的一层气，是大气层；充满房间、包围人的那层感觉，是气氛。

root: 由希腊语 atmos「气、蒸气」与 sphaira「球」构成，字面指包着星球的气层；由包围人的空气引申为场所给人的整体感受。

sensesIntro.en: Something invisible fills and surrounds, whether it is gas or feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 看不见的东西充满并包围四周，它可以是气体，也可以是情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin skin of air around a ball.
core.cn: 核心意象：球体外一层薄薄的气。

intro.en: The second half is the sphere family, and the first half is a Greek word for vapour.
intro.cn: 后半是 sphere 词族，前半是希腊语中表示「气」的词。

latinIntro.en: Greek sphaira reached English through Latin sphaera.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 sphaira 经拉丁语 sphaera 进入英语。

items.meaning: the ball of air around a planet

definition_zh: 大气的；大气造成的；有氛围的、营造气氛的
definition_en: relating to the atmosphere or to conditions in it; also describing something that creates a mood
core_image: 玻璃箱里的空气被一点点抽走，箱盖在外侧气压下缓缓下陷
scene: 实验室的玻璃箱里，空气被一点点抽走，箱壁开始承受内外差压。Atmospheric pressure pushed the lid down as the pump withdrew air.
sceneCN: 这里 atmospheric 指「与大气压有关的」（第 3 个义项：大气压的）；句意为随着泵抽走空气，大气压把盖子压了下去。图中可辨识物件：玻璃箱、真空泵、下陷的盖子、压力表。

derivatives.zh: 在大气方面；从氛围上说

senses.title: Relating to the atmosphere
senses.definition: relating to the gas envelope of a planet
senses.definitionCN: 与行星的气体包层有关
senses.example: Atmospheric layers are named by how temperature changes with height.
senses.exampleCN: 大气各层按温度随高度变化的方式命名。
senses.why: the adjective attaches the noun atmosphere to whatever it describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把名词 atmosphere 挂到它所描述的事物上。

senses.title: Produced in or by the atmosphere
senses.titleCN: 大气中发生的；大气造成的
senses.definition: occurring in the air or caused by processes within it
senses.definitionCN: 发生在空气中，或由其中的过程造成
senses.example: Atmospheric dust dimmed the sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 大气中的尘埃让落日变得黯淡。
senses.why: the envelope is also a workshop, and the adjective marks what goes on inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这层包层也是一间工坊，这个形容词标示在其中发生的事。

senses.title: Of atmospheric pressure
senses.definition: relating to the weight and pressure of the air
senses.definitionCN: 与空气的重量和压强有关
senses.example: Atmospheric pressure pushed the lid down as the pump withdrew air.
senses.exampleCN: 随着泵抽走空气，大气压把盖子压了下去。
senses.why: pressure is the atmosphere's most measurable behaviour, and the adjective marks that use.
senses.whyCN: 压强是大气最可测量的行为，这个形容词标示这一用法。

senses.title: Creating a mood
senses.definition: describing light, sound, design or writing that deliberately creates a mood
senses.definitionCN: 形容有意营造某种情绪的光线、声音、设计或文字
senses.example: The director used fog and low light for an atmospheric opening.
senses.exampleCN: 导演用雾与低照度营造了一个有气氛的开场。
senses.why: designers found that light and fog can wrap a space like air wraps a body.
senses.whyCN: 设计者发现光与雾能像空气包住天体那样包住空间。

senses.title: Having a strong mood
senses.definition: having a distinct and memorable feeling, as a place or a piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 如场所或音乐，具有鲜明而难忘的感觉
senses.example: The empty station was strangely atmospheric at night.
senses.exampleCN: 空荡的车站在夜里有一种奇特的氛围。
senses.why: some places hold a feeling so strongly that the word for air becomes the word for it.
senses.whyCN: 有些地方强烈地留住一种感觉，以至于空气之词变成了感觉之词。

senses.title: Of atmospheric chemistry
senses.definition: relating to the chemical composition and reactions of the air
senses.definitionCN: 与空气的化学组成和反应有关
senses.example: Atmospheric chemistry tracks how ozone forms and breaks down.
senses.exampleCN: 大气化学追踪臭氧如何生成与分解。
senses.why: chemistry inside the air is a subject of its own, and the adjective labels it.
senses.whyCN: 空气内部的化学自成一门课题，这个形容词为它贴标签。

senses.title: Of emissions and pollution
senses.definition: relating to substances released into the air and their effects
senses.definitionCN: 与排入空气的物质及其影响有关
senses.example: Atmospheric carbon reached a new record last year.
senses.exampleCN: 大气中的碳含量去年创下新纪录。
senses.why: what enters the air becomes an atmospheric subject, and policy borrowed the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 进入空气之物成了大气课题，政策也借用这个形容词。

senses.title: Of other worlds' envelopes
senses.definition: relating to the gas envelopes of planets, moons or stars other than the earth
senses.definitionCN: 与地球以外行星、卫星或恒星的气体包层有关
senses.example: Atmospheric models of Titan predict methane rain.
senses.exampleCN: 土卫六的大气模式预测会有甲烷雨。
senses.why: other worlds have envelopes too, and models of them extend the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 其他世界也有包层，对它们的模拟延伸了这个形容词。

intro.en: Atmospheric is atmosphere plus the adjective suffix -ic, which goes back through Latin to Greek. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: atmospheric 是 atmosphere 加形容词后缀 -ic，后者经拉丁语追溯到希腊语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Atmos 'vapour, steam' is of uncertain deeper origin; no reliable Indo-European source is established.
items.cn: atmos「水汽、蒸汽」的更深来源不确定，尚未确立可靠的印欧语来源。

items.en: Sphaira 'ball, globe' gave the second half of the noun atmosphere.
items.cn: sphaira「球、圆球」给出名词 atmosphere 的后半。

items.en: Atmosphaera was coined in seventeenth-century Latin science and passed into English in the 1630s.
items.cn: atmosphaera 在十七世纪拉丁科学中造出，并于十七世纪三十年代进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ic comes from Greek -ikos through Latin -icus; it turns the noun into a relational adjective.
items.cn: 后缀 -ic 经拉丁 -icus 出自希腊 -ikos，把名词变成表示关系的形容词。

items.en: In the nineteenth century atmospheric extended from the physical air to anything that creates or carries a mood.
items.cn: 十九世纪，atmospheric 从物理的空气延伸到一切营造或承载气氛的事物。

items.en: First English date approximate: no exact first use of atmospheric is recorded, and it is usually placed in the late eighteenth or early nineteenth century.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数：atmospheric 的确切首见英语书证未被记录，通常放在十八世纪末或十九世纪初。

note.en: Group one holds closely related forms that are not this adjective; group two holds adjectives for air, weather and mood.
note.cn: 第一组是关系密切、却不是这个形容词的形式；第二组是表示空气、天气与氛围的形容词。

entries.definition: A rare fuller variant of the same adjective, found mainly in older prose.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的罕见完整变体，主要见于较早的文字。

entries.definition: A plural noun for radio noise and mood effects; it is not the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 表示无线电噪声与氛围效果的名词复数，并非这个形容词。

entries.definition: The noun itself; the adjective and the noun are often confused in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词本身；写作中这个形容词与名词常被混用。

entries.definition: A noun phrase built from the adjective; it names one quantity rather than a whole class of things.
entries.definitionCN: 由这个形容词构成的名词短语，指一个量而非一整类事物。

entries.definition: Full of air, light and space; it describes a room's feel, not the gas envelope.
entries.definitionCN: 空气充足、明亮开阔；描述房间的感觉，而非气体包层。

entries.definition: Relating to long-term climate; atmospheric concerns the air and its immediate conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 与长期气候有关；atmospheric 关心空气及其即时状况。

entries.definition: Relating to weather science and forecasting; atmospheric is the broader physical adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 与气象科学与预报有关；atmospheric 是范围更宽的物理形容词。

entries.definition: Bringing a feeling or memory to mind; it overlaps with the mood sense but has no physical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 唤起感觉或记忆；与氛围义重叠，但没有物理含义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: atmosphere plus -ic, the standard relational adjective suffix.
normal.cn: atmosphere 加 -ic，即标准的关系形容词后缀。

normal.en: The family runs atmosphere, atmospheric, atmospherically, atmospherics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 atmosphere、atmospheric、atmospherically、atmospherics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: atmospheric pressure, atmospheric science, atmospheric lighting.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：大气压、大气科学、营造气氛的灯光。

normal.en: The mood sense is modern and common in reviews of films, hotels and music.
normal.cn: 氛围义较现代，常见于电影、酒店与音乐的评论。

normal.en: The rare variant atmospherical is longer but means the same.
normal.cn: 罕见变体 atmospherical 更长，但意思相同。

abstract.en: Picture a glass box whose lid sinks as the pump pulls air out.
abstract.cn: 想象一只玻璃箱，泵抽气时盖子向下陷。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor lit so dimly that every step feels important.
abstract.cn: 想象一条灯光极暗的走廊，每一步都显得重要。

abstract.en: Picture a thin blue line drawn along the edge of a planet.
abstract.cn: 想象沿行星边缘画的一条细蓝线。

examples.en: Atmospheric pressure falls as the weather front approaches.
examples.cn: 随着天气锋面逼近，气压下降。

examples.en: The production was praised for its atmospheric design.
examples.cn: 这部制作因营造气氛的设计受到称赞。

examples.en: Atmospheric models help predict conditions on other planets.
examples.cn: 大气模式有助于预测其他行星上的状况。

dict_mnemonic.text: atmosphere 是大气，-ic 是形容词后缀：大气的；后来人们把「有空气感」引申为「有氛围的」

root: 希腊 atmos「水汽」+ sphaira「球」→ 现代拉丁 atmosphaera → 英语 atmosphere；加 -ic（经拉丁 -icus 出自希腊 -ikos）→ atmospheric。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective outward: the envelope, what happens inside it, its pressure, the moods it can create, strong atmosphere, its chemistry, its emissions and the envelopes of other worlds.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形容词向外展开：气体包层、其中发生的事、它的压强、它能营造的情绪、浓烈的气氛、它的化学、它的排放，以及其他世界的气体包层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin blue line drawn along the edge of a planet.
core.cn: 核心意象：沿行星边缘画的一条细蓝线。

branches.en: THE SHELL NEAR AND FAR: the same adjective covers our envelope and those of other bodies.
branches.cn: 近处与远处的外壳：同一个形容词既指我们这层，也指其他天体的那层。

branches.en: WHAT HAPPENS INSIDE: dust, chemistry and emissions are all processes within the air.
branches.cn: 其中发生的事：尘埃、化学与排放都是空气内部的过程。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: pressure is the envelope's most measurable behaviour.
branches.cn: 重量：压强是这层包层最可测量的行为。

branches.en: THE CRAFTED MOOD: light and sound can be arranged to wrap a space.
branches.cn: 刻意营造的氛围：光与声可以被安排来包住一个空间。

branches.en: THE MOOD THAT ARRIVES: some places hold a feeling without anyone arranging it.
branches.cn: 自然降临的氛围：有些地方无需安排就留住一种感觉。

intro.en: Atmospheric is a noun plus one suffix, and both halves are shared with a large scientific family.
intro.cn: atmospheric 是一个名词加一个后缀，两半都与一个庞大的科学词族共用。

latinIntro.en: Modern Latin atmosphaera supplies the noun, and Latin -icus from Greek -ikos supplies the adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 现代拉丁 atmosphaera 提供名词，拉丁 -icus（出自希腊 -ikos）提供形容词词尾。

items.example: The first piece names the gas.
The second piece gives the shape.
Atmospheric pressure pushed the lid down.
items.exampleCN: 大气压把盖子压了下去。
这个山谷在大气上受到屏障。

items.example: The storm filled the radio with atmospherics.
items.exampleCN: 风暴让收音机满是大气干扰。
较早的书更爱用这一完整形式。

items.meaning: a rare synonym for the envelope
items.meaningCN: 空气包层的罕见同义词
items.example: Aerosphere is mostly a historical term.
items.exampleCN: 这个词多半是历史术语。

latinEntries.meaning: the envelope of air around a body

definition_zh: 环礁；珊瑚环礁（由珊瑚礁围成环形、中间包着潟湖的海岛）
definition_en: a ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a shallow lagoon, often with low islets on the rim
core_image: 海面上一圈细细的白浪围住一片浅蓝，圈外是深蓝，圈内是平静的浅水
scene: 飞机下降时，海面浮出一圈白色浪线，中间围着一片浅蓝水面。Below them an atoll ringed a shallow lagoon.
sceneCN: 这里 atoll 指「环形珊瑚礁及其围合的整体」（第 1 个义项：作为完整地貌单位的环礁）；句意为他们下方的一座环礁围着一片浅潟湖。

pos.zh: 环礁；珊瑚环礁（可数，复数 atolls）

derivatives.zh: atoll（环礁）+ lagoon（潟湖，意大利 laguna ← 拉丁 lacuna「水池」）→ 环礁潟湖：环礁围出的浅水区
atoll + reef（礁，古诺斯语 rif「脊」）→ 环礁礁体：构成环形的珊瑚礁带
cay（小沙岛，源自西班牙语 cayo，可能上溯加勒比语）→ 环礁礁缘上的低矮沙洲
atoll + -like（类似……的）→ 环礁状的：形状像环礁的

senses.title: A ring-shaped reef
senses.titleCN: 环形礁体：围合的整体地貌
senses.definition: a coral reef forming a closed or nearly closed ring
senses.definitionCN: 形成闭合或近于闭合环形的珊瑚礁
senses.example: Below them an atoll ringed a shallow lagoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们下方的一座环礁围着一片浅潟湖。
senses.why: the word names the whole ring, not one part of it, because the ring is what makes the feature recognisable from the air.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名整个环，而非其中一部分，因为从空中辨认靠的正是这个环。

senses.title: The reef rim
senses.definition: the outer edge of the reef where waves break
senses.definitionCN: 礁体迎浪的外缘，即白浪破碎处
senses.example: Surf broke along the atoll rim all night.
senses.exampleCN: 整夜都有浪沿着环礁礁缘破碎。
senses.why: the rim is the part that meets the open ocean, so the word is used for the outer edge as well as for the whole ring.
senses.whyCN: 礁缘是与外海相接的部分，因此这个词也指外缘，而不只指整个环。

senses.title: The enclosed lagoon
senses.titleCN: 环内潟湖：被围住的浅水
senses.definition: the shallow water enclosed by the ring
senses.definitionCN: 被环礁围住的浅水区
senses.example: The atoll holds a lagoon barely ten metres deep.
senses.exampleCN: 这座环礁围出一个不足十米深的潟湖。
senses.why: the ring exists by enclosing something, so the enclosed water is treated as part of the atoll's description.
senses.whyCN: 环的意义在于围住什么，因此被围的水也被视为环礁描述的一部分。

senses.title: Islets on the rim
senses.definition: low sandy islets built on parts of the reef
senses.definitionCN: 在礁体部分地段堆起的低矮沙岛
senses.example: Three islets rise only two metres above the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 环礁上的三座小岛只高出海面两米。
senses.why: sand and coral rubble collect on the rim, so the word also names the land that the reef carries.
senses.whyCN: 沙与珊瑚碎屑堆在礁缘，因此这个词也命名礁体承载的陆地。

senses.title: Formation by subsidence
senses.titleCN: 成因：火山基座沉降与珊瑚上长
senses.definition: the geological history in which a volcanic base subsides while coral grows upward
senses.definitionCN: 火山基座下沉、珊瑚向上生长所形成的地质历史
senses.example: Darwin explained the atoll by slow subsidence of a volcanic base.
senses.exampleCN: 达尔文用火山基座的缓慢沉降解释环礁的成因。
senses.why: the ring shape records a history: coral keeps building at the edge while the centre sinks.
senses.whyCN: 环形记录了一段历史：珊瑚在边缘持续建造，中央则在下沉。

senses.title: A human home
senses.titleCN: 人类居所：低岛上的生活
senses.definition: the land and water used as a home by island communities
senses.definitionCN: 被岛上社群当作居所的陆与水
senses.example: The atoll supports a fishing village of two hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 这座环礁供养着一个两百人的渔村。
senses.why: a ring of islets with sheltered water is a practical place to live, so the word also names a human territory.
senses.whyCN: 一圈小岛加一片受护的水面是实用的居所，因此这个词也命名人类的地域。

senses.title: An ancient limestone body
senses.titleCN: 古环礁：抬升后的石灰岩体
senses.definition: a fossil atoll uplifted and exposed as limestone
senses.definitionCN: 被抬升出露、成为石灰岩的化石环礁
senses.example: The quarry cuts through an ancient atoll.
senses.exampleCN: 采石场切穿一座古环礁。
senses.why: when the seafloor rises, the reef becomes solid rock, and geology keeps the name for the fossil shape.
senses.whyCN: 海底抬升后礁体变成坚硬的岩石，地质学仍用这个词称呼那个化石形状。

senses.title: A low, exposed coast
senses.titleCN: 低洼而脆弱的环礁海岸
senses.definition: the atoll considered as a low-lying coast vulnerable to waves and rising sea
senses.definitionCN: 作为低洼、易受浪与海面上涨影响的环礁海岸
senses.example: Rising seas threaten every atoll in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 海面上涨威胁着这个地区的每一座环礁。
senses.why: the land sits only metres above the sea, so the word has become a shorthand for that vulnerability.
senses.whyCN: 陆地只高出海面数米，因此这个词已成为那种脆弱性的代称。

intro.en: Atoll entered English through French from Dhivehi, the language of the Maldives, where atolu names a reef ring. It has no Latin ancestry. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: atoll 经法语从马尔代夫的迪维希语进入英语，当地语 atolu 指环形礁。它没有拉丁语祖先。年代均为约数。

items.en: Atolu in Dhivehi named the ring reefs of the Maldive islands, a navigational fact long known to local sailors.
items.cn: 迪维希语 atolu 指马尔代夫群岛的环形礁，这是当地水手早已知晓的航行事实。

items.en: French naturalists adopted the word in the early nineteenth century as atoll, spelling it after their own conventions.
items.cn: 十九世纪初法国博物学家借入这个词作 atoll，并按法语习惯拼写。

items.en: English took atoll from French in the 1830s, at first only for the Maldive and Caroline rings.
items.cn: 英语于十九世纪三十年代从法语借入 atoll，最初只用于马尔代夫与加罗林群岛的环礁。

items.en: Darwin's subsidence theory of 1842 gave the word a geological definition and spread it through science.
items.cn: 达尔文一八四二年的沉降说赋予这个词地质定义，并使它在科学界传播。

items.en: Twentieth-century oceanography mapped atolls worldwide and added the climate sense of a low, exposed coast.
items.cn: 二十世纪海洋学测绘了全球环礁，并加入「低洼脆弱海岸」的气候义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Dhivehi source of atolu is not established, and any Sanskrit or Indo-Aryan form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源存疑）：atolu 在迪维希语之前的来源无定论，凡为其给出的梵语或印度-雅利安语形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the reef types routinely confused with an atoll; group two holds the general landform words nearby in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是常与环礁混淆的礁类型；第二组是语义相近的一般地貌词。

entries.definition: A reef running parallel to a coast and separated from it by a lagoon; it does not close into a ring.
entries.definitionCN: 与海岸平行、被潟湖隔开的礁带；它并不闭合成环。

entries.definition: A reef growing directly along a coastline with no lagoon between it and the land.
entries.definitionCN: 紧贴海岸生长、与陆地之间没有潟湖的礁。

entries.definition: The shallow water enclosed by a reef or sandbar; an atoll contains a lagoon but is not one.
entries.definitionCN: 被礁或沙洲围住的浅水；环礁包含潟湖，但它本身不是潟湖。

entries.definition: A small low sandy island on a reef; it is one piece of an atoll's rim, not the whole ring.
entries.definitionCN: 礁上的低矮小沙岛；它只是环礁礁缘的一小段，不是整个环。

entries.definition: Any ridge of rock or coral near the surface; it need not form a ring and need not enclose water.
entries.definitionCN: 任何接近水面的岩脊或珊瑚脊；不必成环，也不必围住水。

entries.definition: A piece of land surrounded by water; it says nothing about coral or about a ring shape.
entries.definitionCN: 四周被水围住的陆地；不涉及珊瑚，也不涉及环形。

entries.definition: A group or chain of islands; it is a regional grouping, not a single ring reef.
entries.definitionCN: 一组或一串岛屿；它是区域性的岛群，不是单个环形礁。

entries.definition: A shallow area of sand or rock rising near the surface; it has no enclosing ring.
entries.definitionCN: 接近水面隆起的浅沙或浅岩区；没有围合的环。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real geography, real reef types and real formation steps, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的地貌、真实的礁类型与真实的形成步骤，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Atoll is a borrowed Pacific word, not a Latin one: the thing and the name travel together.
normal.cn: atoll 是借来的太平洋词汇，不是拉丁词：事物与名字一起传来。

normal.en: The shape is a ring: reef outside, lagoon inside, islets on the rim.
normal.cn: 形状是一个环：外面是礁，里面是潟湖，环上散着小岛。

normal.en: Formation order: volcano, fringing reef, barrier reef, atoll, as the base sinks.
normal.cn: 形成次序：火山、裙礁、堡礁、环礁，随基座下沉而演进。

normal.en: An atoll is not a lagoon: the atoll is the ring, the lagoon is the water inside it.
normal.cn: 环礁不是潟湖：环礁是那个环，潟湖是环里的水。

normal.en: Low elevation is the point: most atoll islets stand only a few metres above the sea.
normal.cn: 低海拔是关键：多数环礁小岛只高出海面几米。

abstract.en: An atoll is a reef that learned to draw a circle around its own disappearance.
abstract.cn: 环礁是一座学会围着自己消失之处画圈的礁。

abstract.en: It is a ring of stone keeping a shallow promise of safety.
abstract.cn: 它是一圈石头，守着一份浅浅的安全承诺。

abstract.en: The volcano is gone, and only its coral handwriting remains.
abstract.cn: 火山已经不在了，只剩它珊瑚写下的笔迹。

examples.en: The atoll is less than three metres above sea level at its highest point.
examples.cn: 这座环礁最高处不足海拔三米。

examples.en: Coral grew upward as the volcanic base of the atoll subsided.
examples.cn: 随着环礁的火山基座下沉，珊瑚向上生长。

examples.en: Fresh water lies in a thin lens beneath the atoll.
examples.cn: 环礁之下有一层薄薄的淡水透镜。

dict_mnemonic.text: atoll＝环礁；记成「一圈礁围着中间浅水」，成因是火山下沉、珊瑚上长，外面浪白，里面水静。

root: 借自迪维希语 atolu（环形礁），经法语 atoll 进入英语；无拉丁语源，迪维希语之前的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one ring: the whole reef, its rim, its lagoon, its islets, its subsidence history, its human home, its fossil limestone body and its exposed coast.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个环展开：整圈礁、礁缘、潟湖、小岛、沉降历史、人类居所、化石石灰岩体与脆弱海岸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin white ring of breaking waves around a pale blue centre, with deep blue outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈细白浪线围着一片浅蓝，圈外是深蓝。

branches.en: RING AND RIM: the whole circle, then the outer edge where waves break.
branches.cn: 环与缘：先是整个圈，再是迎浪的外缘。

branches.en: WATER AND LAND INSIDE: the enclosed lagoon, then the islets on the rim.
branches.cn: 圈内的水与陆：先是被围的潟湖，再是礁缘的小岛。

branches.en: HISTORY IN STONE: subsidence explains the ring, and uplift turns it into limestone.
branches.cn: 石中的历史：沉降解释环的形成，抬升又把它变成石灰岩。

branches.en: HUMAN HOME: the ring becomes a territory with a village and a fishery.
branches.cn: 人类居所：环变成有村庄与渔场的领地。

branches.en: LOW COAST: the same ring is now a measure of vulnerability.
branches.cn: 低海岸：同一个环如今成了脆弱性的尺度。

intro.en: Atoll is a single borrowed noun with no internal morphology; its related vocabulary comes from geography and other languages.
intro.cn: atoll 是单一借入名词，内部没有构词结构；它的相关词汇来自地理学与其他语言。

latinIntro.en: Atoll has no Latin entries. Latin insula 'island' and Greek korallion 'coral' describe the same setting from unrelated roots.
latinIntro.cn: atoll 没有拉丁条目。拉丁 insula「岛」与希腊 korallion「珊瑚」用无关词根描述同一环境。

items.exampleCN: 这座环礁远离任何大陆。

items.exampleCN: 珊瑚用千年时间造出这个环。

definition_zh: 原子；微粒；一点点
definition_en: the smallest unit of a chemical element, or a very small amount
core_image: 一颗小到不能再切开的小球
scene: 黑板上画着电子绕着中心转的圈。The atom has a nucleus at its centre.
sceneCN: 这里 atom 是「原子」（第 1 个义项：构成元素的基本微粒）；句意是原子中心有一个原子核。

derivatives.zh: 动词：使雾化；使分裂成微粒

senses.title: Smallest unit of an element
senses.definition: the smallest unit of a chemical element that can take part in a reaction
senses.definitionCN: 能参与化学反应的最小元素单位
senses.example: The atom has a nucleus at its centre.
senses.exampleCN: 原子中心有一个原子核。
senses.why: Atom comes from Greek atomos, 'uncut', from a- 'not' plus temnein 'to cut', because the ancients thought it could not be divided further.
senses.whyCN: atom 来自希腊语 atomos「不可切分的」，由 a-「不」与 temnein「切」构成，因为古人以为它小到不能再分。

senses.title: A very small amount
senses.definition: a very small amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 极少的一点分量
senses.example: There is not an atom of truth in the rumour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个传言里没有一点真实成分。
senses.why: The smallest unit of matter became a measure of the smallest possible amount, used for emphasis in negatives.
senses.whyCN: 物质的最小单位被借来度量最小可能的分量，多用于否定句以加强语气。

senses.why: Because the first large-scale use of this energy was described as atomic, the adjective widened from the particle to the power released from it.

definition_zh: n. 萎缩（组织或器官因缺乏使用或营养而变小）；v. 萎缩；衰退
definition_en: The wasting away of a body part through lack of use or nourishment; as a verb, to waste away, or of a skill or institution, to decline from neglect.
core_image: 一条腿细了一圈，像久不浇水而缩掉的枝条
scene: 卧床数月让他小腿的肌肉明显萎缩。Months in bed caused muscle atrophy in his legs.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：atrophy 指组织或器官因不用或失养而萎缩变小。

senses.title: The wasting of body tissue
senses.definition: the shrinking of an organ or tissue because it is not used or not properly nourished
senses.definitionCN: 器官或组织因缺乏使用或营养不足而变小
senses.example: The scan showed atrophy in the left hemisphere.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示左半球有萎缩。
senses.why: The root means nourishment and the prefix removes it, so the word literally says no feeding.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「营养」，前缀把它取消，所以这个词字面上就是「没有喂养」。

senses.title: To decline from neglect
senses.definition: as a verb, to waste away, used of muscles and equally of skills, habits or institutions
senses.definitionCN: 作动词指萎缩，既用于肌肉，也用于技能、习惯或制度
senses.example: Unused languages atrophy within a few years.
senses.exampleCN: 不用的语言几年内就会退化。
senses.why: The body picture transfers easily: anything left unfed grows smaller, whether a limb or a committee.
senses.whyCN: 身体的画面很容易迁移：任何不被喂养的东西都会变小，无论一条肢体还是一个委员会。

intro.en: Atrophy is Greek atrophia, from a-, without, and trophe, nourishment, from trephein, to nourish: literally the state of not being fed.
intro.cn: atrophy 就是希腊语 atrophia，由 a-「无」与 trophe「营养」构成，后者出自 trephein「滋养」：字面就是「不被喂养的状态」。

items.en: Greek trephein meant to nourish or rear, used of feeding children and animals.
items.cn: 希腊语 trephein 意为「滋养、养育」，用于喂养孩子与牲畜。

items.en: The noun trophe meant nourishment or food, the root of the whole trophic family.
items.cn: 名词 trophe 意为「营养、食物」，是整个「营养」词族的词根。

items.en: With a-, without, atrophia named the condition of a part that gets no nourishment.
items.cn: 加上 a-「无」后，atrophia 指某个部位得不到营养的状态。

items.en: Medical Latin kept the Greek term and spread it through European textbooks.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语沿用这个希腊词，并通过欧洲教科书传播。

items.en: English records atrophy from the sixteenth century as a noun of wasting.
items.cn: 英语从十六世纪起记录 atrophy，作为表示萎缩的名词。

items.en: The verb use spread in the nineteenth century, and writers soon applied it to skills and institutions.
items.cn: 动词用法在十九世纪扩展，作者很快把它用于技能与制度。

note.en: The look-alike group is the whole nourishment family plus two words that only sound alike; the near-meaning group lists kinds of decline.
note.cn: 形近组是整个「营养」词族加上两个只是音近的词；近义组列出各种衰退。

entries.definition: Excessive growth of a tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 组织的过度增长。

entries.definition: A disorder of poor nourishment of tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 组织营养障碍性疾病。

entries.definition: A prize kept as a sign of victory.
entries.definitionCN: 作为胜利标志留存的奖品。

entries.definition: The punctuation mark showing omission.
entries.definitionCN: 表示省略的标点符号。

entries.definition: The gradual loss of body tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 身体组织的逐渐流失。

entries.definition: A gradual fall in strength or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 力量或质量的逐渐下降。

entries.definition: A worsening of structure or function.
entries.definitionCN: 结构或功能的恶化。

entries.definition: The process of becoming smaller.
entries.definitionCN: 变小的过程。

normalIntro.en: Atrophy is a-, without, plus troph, nourishment: no feeding, so the part grows smaller.
normalIntro.cn: atrophy 就是 a-「无」加 troph「营养」：没有喂养，于是那个部位变小。

normal.en: Hypertrophy is too much growth, atrophy too little.
normal.cn: hypertrophy 是长过头，atrophy 是长不足。

normal.en: Dystrophy is bad feeding, not no feeding.
normal.cn: dystrophy 是喂养不良，不是不喂养。

normal.en: The verb forms are atrophies, atrophied, atrophying.
normal.cn: 动词形式是 atrophies、atrophied、atrophying。

normal.en: Trophy is unrelated, from a Greek word for turning.
normal.cn: trophy 无亲缘，出自希腊语「转向」。

normal.en: Skills atrophy just as muscles do.
normal.cn: 技能与肌肉一样会退化。

abstract.en: Picture a branch shrinking on an unwatered plant.
abstract.cn: 想象久不浇水的植株上缩掉的枝条。

abstract.en: Imagine a leg noticeably thinner than the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一条明显比另一条细的腿。

abstract.en: Think of a committee nobody feeds with work.
abstract.cn: 想象一个没人给它活干的委员会。

examples.en: Bed rest leads to rapid atrophy.
examples.cn: 卧床会导致迅速萎缩。

examples.en: His shoulder muscles had atrophied.
examples.cn: 他的肩部肌肉已经萎缩。

examples.en: Without practice the skill will atrophy.
examples.cn: 不加练习，这项技能就会退化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「无」+ troph「营养」+ -y「状态」——断了营养的状态，就是萎缩 atrophy。

root: 希腊语 trephein「滋养」生出 trophe「营养」，加否定前缀 a- 成 atrophia「失养」，经医学拉丁语入十六世纪英语；同根还有 hypertrophy 与 dystrophy。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one unfed thing shrinking: a muscle without use, and a skill or institution without work.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是同一个「断粮之物」在缩小：不用的肌肉，以及没有活干的技能或制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a leg grown thinner, like a branch on an unwatered plant
core.cn: 核心意象：一条腿细了一圈，像久不浇水而缩掉的枝条

intro.en: Atrophy is a-, without, troph-, nourishment, and -y; the same root builds hypertrophy, dystrophy and trophic.
intro.cn: atrophy 由 a-「无」、troph-「营养」与 -y 构成；同一词根还构成 hypertrophy、dystrophy 与 trophic。

latinIntro.en: The classical layer is Greek trophe, nourishment, matched by Latin nutrire, to feed, and alimentum, food.
latinIntro.cn: 古典层次是希腊语 trophe「营养」，对应拉丁语 nutrire「喂养」与 alimentum「食物」。

latinEntries.exampleCN: trophe 是「营养」词族的起点。

definition_zh: 系上；附上；认为有（重要性）
definition_en: to fasten one thing to another, or to connect value or feeling to it
core_image: 用别针把两张纸别在一起
scene: 填表时她随手把照片别在右上角。She attached a photo to the form.
sceneCN: 这里 attach 是「附上」（第 1 个义项：把东西固定到另一件东西上）；句意是她把照片附在表格上。

senses.title: Fasten one thing to another
senses.definition: to fasten or join one thing to another
senses.definitionCN: 把一件东西固定或连接到另一件上
senses.example: She attached a photo to the form.
senses.exampleCN: 她把照片附在表格上。
senses.why: Attach comes from Old French atachier, 'to fasten with a nail', so the original act is pinning one object onto another.
senses.whyCN: attach 来自古法语 atachier「用钉子固定」，最初的动作就是把一件东西钉到另一件上。

senses.title: Treat as important
senses.definition: to connect value or importance to something
senses.definitionCN: 把价值或重要性系在某事上
senses.example: The school attaches great importance to reading.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校非常重视阅读。
senses.why: Pinning a value onto a thing is a short step from pinning a label on it, so the physical fastening becomes a judgement of worth.
senses.whyCN: 把价值钉在某物上，与把标签钉在实物上只差一步，于是具体的固定动作变成了对价值的判断。

senses.title: Be emotionally tied
senses.definition: to feel affection that ties you to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 因感情而与某人某物系在一起
senses.example: She is deeply attached to her old bike.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那辆旧自行车很有感情。
senses.why: Affection works like a rope: being attached means the tie is felt rather than seen, ending in the passive form used for fondness.
senses.whyCN: 感情像一根绳：be attached 表示这根绳看不见却能感到，于是被动形式专门用来表示依恋。

intro.en: Attach began as a word about nailing things down and grew senses of value and affection.
intro.cn: attach 起初指用钉子固定，后来长出价值与感情方面的含义。

items.en: tache meant 'a nail or fastening'.
items.cn: tache 意为「钉子、扣件」。

items.en: atachier meant 'to fasten or pin'.
items.cn: atachier 意为「固定、别住」。

items.en: attachen first meant 'to seize legally'.
items.cn: attachen 最初还有「依法扣押」之义。

items.en: The word settled on fastening things together.
items.cn: 词义固定为把东西连接在一起。

items.en: Attach importance to and be attached to developed as fixed uses.
items.cn: 重视与依恋两种说法逐渐固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group is the attach family; the near-meaning group gives verbs of joining.
note.cn: 形近组是 attach 词族；近义组是表示连接的动词。

normalIntro.en: Attach pins one thing to another, and can pin value or feeling too.
normalIntro.cn: attach 把一件东西别到另一件上，也能把价值或感情别上去。

normal.en: The pattern is attach something to something.
normal.cn: 常用结构是 attach something to something。

normal.en: Attach importance to is a formal way to say value.
normal.cn: attach importance to 是「重视」的正式说法。

normal.en: Be attached to usually means feel fond of.
normal.cn: be attached to 通常表示依恋。

normal.en: The double t comes from the prefix and stem meeting.
normal.cn: 双 t 来自前缀与词干相接。

normal.en: The word ends with a ch sound.
normal.cn: 词尾读作 ch 音。

abstract.cn: 想象一个回形针把两页纸别住。

abstract.en: See a price tag tied to a handle.
abstract.cn: 想象价签系在把手上。

abstract.en: See an invisible cord from a hand to an old object.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手与旧物之间有一根看不见的线。

examples.cn: 她把照片附在表格上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 古法语 atachier 是「钉住」：把东西钉在一起是附上；把价值钉在某事上是重视；把感情钉在某人身上是依恋。

root: 源自 Old French atachier「用钉子固定」，词根 tache 意为钉子；由具体的「别住、连上」引申为赋予价值，再引申为情感上的依恋。

sensesIntro.en: A pin, a value and an affection are all things tied to something else.
sensesIntro.cn: 别针、价值与感情，都是系在别的东西上的东西。

core.cn: 核心意象：一根别针穿过两页纸。

intro.en: The prefix a- here comes from Latin ad-, and detach reverses the act.
intro.cn: 这里的前缀 a- 来自拉丁语 ad-，而 detach 表示相反的动作。

latinIntro.en: The stem goes back to a Germanic word for a nail, borrowed into French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干可追溯到日耳曼语中表示钉子的词，后被法语借用。

definition_zh: 攻击；抨击；（疾病）发作
definition_en: to use force against someone, to criticize strongly, or a sudden onset of illness
core_image: 一只手突然伸向对方
scene: 报纸头版猛烈批评了这项决定。The paper attacked the decision on its front page.
sceneCN: 这里 attack 是「抨击」（第 2 个义项：用言语猛烈批评）；句意是报纸在头版抨击这项决定。

senses.title: Use force against
senses.definition: to try to hurt or defeat someone with force
senses.definitionCN: 用武力伤害或击败对方
senses.example: The soldiers attacked the bridge at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们在黎明时进攻那座桥。
senses.why: Attack comes from Italian attaccare, 'to join battle', from a word meaning to fasten, so the core picture is closing with an enemy and engaging.
senses.whyCN: attack 来自意大利语 attaccare「接上打斗」，其词根意为「接合」，所以核心画面是贴近敌人、交上手。

senses.title: Criticize strongly
senses.definition: to criticize someone or something very strongly in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在言语或文字中猛烈批评某人某事
senses.example: The paper attacked the decision on its front page.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸在头版抨击这项决定。
senses.why: A verbal assault borrows the whole martial image: words are aimed and driven at a target as if they were blows.
senses.whyCN: 言语上的攻击借用了整套交战画面：话像拳头一样被瞄准并砸向目标。

senses.title: Sudden onset of illness
senses.definition: a sudden and severe start of an illness
senses.definitionCN: 疾病突然而猛烈地开始
senses.example: He had a heart attack last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他去年冬天心脏病发作。
senses.why: Illness arrives like an enemy raid, so its sudden onset is named with the same word as a military strike.
senses.whyCN: 疾病像敌军突袭一样到来，所以它突然开始的那一刻，就用与军事打击相同的词来命名。

intro.en: Attack entered English from Italian fighting speech and spread from battle to words and illness.
intro.cn: attack 从意大利语的交战用语进入英语，又从战场扩展到言语与疾病。

items.en: attaccare meant 'to join battle'.
items.cn: attaccare 意为「接战、交上手」。

items.en: The phrase meant 'to begin a fight'.
items.cn: 这一短语意为「开始战斗」。

items.en: attaquer carried the military sense into French.
items.cn: attaquer 把军事含义带入法语。

items.en: English attack covered armed assault.
items.cn: 英语 attack 指武装攻击。

items.en: The word extended to criticism and to illness.
items.cn: 词义扩展到批评与疾病发作。

note.en: The look-alike group is the attack family; the near-meaning group gives verbs of striking and criticizing.
note.cn: 形近组是 attack 词族；近义组是表示打击与批评的动词。
